The row lists [FFI-56] for the C function pointer's message; the std_function message in [FFI-17a] is listed the same way.

judgements.final_cost_row: No row of §X.4 changes and none is added. The limit is decided when the declaration, overlay entry or typedef is compiled, from types the compiler already has, under the existing row "Contract and range-type annotations | not observable | compile time only"; the call that replaces a refused safe call is the one direct call of the existing row "FFI call | guaranteed present | one direct call for an ABI-direct C function" ([FFI-9]: "`extern \"C\"` is the platform C ABI"), and the `extend` wrapper fills the struct from the span's pointer and length, the stores C itself writes to build the struct, and inlines to the same instructions (a cross-package wrapper not inlined costs the one extra call [FFI-29c] already prices for a shim, removed by LTO). A `std_function` value's call keeps the thunk [FFI-17f] already reports; `unsafe fn(A…) -> R` against `fn(A…) -> R` changes no instruction. To measure: `clear(ref mut frame)` against a hand-written C call with the same pointer and length, both compilers, same flags; expected identical time and code size.
judgements.owner_verdicts_touched: None overridden. Verdict 60 (anything that can break a safety promise only inside `unsafe`): applied; the route is closed and the call happens only in `unsafe:`. Verdicts 120, 125, 130, 133, 136: every refused assertion becomes `@safety("…")` above `unsafe fn`, in a hand declaration, an overlay entry or a C++ member's entry; `unsafe` stays no word of `@ffi(…)`; `safe` is [FFI-11]'s existing word; no plain line silently means unsafe, since a plain entry that cannot be made safe is refused where it is written (the method-4 team's decision 3a), and an entry whose written words already leave its calls unsafe (`TODO(…)`, `retained` on a plain pointer) is kept as the current text has it. Verdict 132's lesson: a plain overlay line keeps its written meaning and is never quietly made unsafe by a header field its reader does not see. Verdict 137: results are outside the limit, untouched. Verdict 121: an entry refused in another package's overlay fails every build that applies it, with the `override` line ([FFI-30c]). Verdict 73 and [DIA-25]: every line a message gives compiles, and messages elsewhere offer an assertion only where the limit allows it; [DIA-9] is met by giving the `safe` line conditionally beside the `unsafe:` block, as [FFI-10] and [FFI-40] already do. Verdicts 31, 118, 119, 165: untouched. Delegated rulings: ODR-073 (its reason is the limit's reason; the slot sentence kept word for word), ODR-074 (an unsafe hand declaration keeps its C ABI parameters), ODR-075 and ODR-076 (`ref_to_ptr` and `null[P]()` stay safe; only handing the value to foreign code under an assertion of safety is refused), ODR-115 (`unsafe fn(…) -> R` is the type a `std_function` value takes), ODR-199 (kept in substance, changed in shape: the value's default type becomes `unsafe fn(A…) -> R`, with `safe` on the entry giving `fn(A…) -> R`; a delegated ruling, not an owner verdict, and the method-4 team's decision 4 option (a), which it left for the owner; reported as the one change that refuses programs 0.9.20_Hardened_2 accepts, a call of a `std_function` value outside `unsafe:` without `safe` on its entry, in the spirit of N75: every change of 0.9.20 is a refusal, and `ember fmt --migrate` rewrites nothing).
judgements.remaining_doubt: 1. The dual route is not K07's and stays open for K08's lead: an `@unsafe(export(…))` function ([FFI-26]; [FFI-31b] lists no raw-pointer result among the refused) or an `override fn` of a C++ virtual ([FFI-39]) may return `ref_to_ptr(ref mut local)` in safe code, and C writes through it; [FFI-21a] covers only a pointer into a copied parameter (E5042). The same property applies: a function foreign code calls whose result carries a raw pointer is written `unsafe fn` with `@safety`. 2. Including C function pointers in the limit refuses a plain entry taking an imported ops table even when the program fills it with Ember functions, since an imported field is typed `unsafe extern "C" fn` ([FFI-8]) and types cannot tell the origin; a hand-declared `@layout(c) struct` with safe `extern "C" fn` fields keeps a safe entry. Most such tables also hold a `void* user_data`, refused anyway. If the lead judges the structural route too exotic, dropping the clause "or a C function pointer (`unsafe extern "C" fn(…)`, `[FFI-56]`)" and the words "or C function pointer" in the registry row leaves designs 1 and 3's reach, with the route named here as a gap. 3. [FFI-11]'s `retained` row ("the call stays `unsafe`, with a raw pointer") and [FFI-11c] (a plain entry with `TODO(…)` whose "calls stay `unsafe`") are verdict-130 leftovers: a function unsafe to call written as a plain entry. The trigger qualifier keeps them as they are; aligning them (design 1's row edit, plus FFI-11c) is a question of its own, not K07's, since `ember bind --init` already writes such entries `unsafe fn` ([CLI-5]). 4. [FFI-8]'s table has no row for `void*`/`const void*`; the refusal of `pNext` assumes it maps to a raw pointer type, as any mapping of `void*` must. 5. `@ffi(handle)` values are outside the limit, so a pointer-cast macro constant of a handle type (`((HANDLE)-1)`, [FFI-6a]) still reaches C through a struct in safe code; K46 (J8-14) decides what a handle constant is. 6. [CLI-6] and [CLI-7] count declarations safe or unsafe without naming the limit; the compile refuses the entry, so no program is accepted, but a one-line cite there is cheap if the lead wants the counts to agree. 7. The `@safety` text for `vkCreateBuffer` and the quoted messages are the lead's to word (verdict 157); the lines they give compile under [DIA-25] in every spelling. 8. The E5002 message's line numbers (3, 12) refer to the refused program as design 2 lays it out (struct field on line 3, the call on line 12); the lead may renumber if the example in the text differs.

rulings.title: Can AnyError, Result, a channel or a scoped task carry an error type across threads when that error holds an object of an open class another package may derive from?

designs.question: K20: Can AnyError, Result, a channel or a scoped task carry an error type across threads when that error holds an object of an open class another package may derive from? In particular: how are Send and ThreadShared judged for an open class, and for a value holding one, so that a dependant's subclass cannot break a library's judgement (separate compilation, [BLD-16]), and what are Error's requirements and AnyError's markers?
designs.summary: A value held by the type of an `open` or `abstract` class is type-erased exactly as `dyn I` and `fn()` are, and the text already decides those two by a word on the type (`[THR-8]`: "`dyn I` when `I` requires it (`interface I: needs Send:`)"; verdict 61: `thread_shared fn()`, the owner choosing the word over "the compiler finding it from the whole program"), and `[MOD-9]` says "Where a word exists to write a fact, only the written word counts across the edge". So the ruling gives the open class's markers a word: an `open` or `abstract` class writes `implements Send, ThreadShared` (the grammar's existing `implements` list, without `unsafe`), its objects held by base type have exactly the markers it declares, and every class derived from it, in any package or reload, meets them with its own fields or is refused where it is declared (`E2040`), while a class that cannot be subclassed stays inferred from its fields. On that footing `Error` requires `Send` and `ThreadShared` (any thread may have an error), so `dyn Error`, `AnyError` and every `Result[T]` cross threads by every route with nothing written, and nothing runs for any of it while the program runs.

edits.old: cannot be overridden. Base fields are laid out first; there is at most one base.
edits.new: cannot be overridden. Base fields are laid out first; there is at most one base. **An object held by the type of an `open` or `abstract` class may be of any class derived from it, in any package** (`[TYP-5]` rule 8), which the holder's package never sees (`[BLD-16]`); so what a holder may rely on of such a value is what the class declares, never what its own fields happen to hold: the interfaces it implements, the marker interfaces `Send` and `ThreadShared` included (`pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`, written there without `unsafe`, `[TYP-43]`), each of which every class derived from it meets, checked where that class is declared (`[IFC-3]`, `[THR-8]`, `[THR-9]`). A class that cannot be subclassed is judged from its fields, as a struct is.
edits.why: This is where `open` and `abstract` are defined, and the cause: the kind of such an object is erased from its holder, and the text judged it from the declared class's fields alone, a judgement a dependant's subclass could break. Stating it as a declared promise makes the fact one `[MOD-9]`'s written-word rule already carries across the edge, so no whole-program fact enters any package's code.

edits.old:
Structs, enums, tuples, fixed arrays, collections and class objects
  are `Send` when every component is;
edits.new: Structs, enums, tuples, fixed arrays, collections and objects of a class that cannot be subclassed (`[CLS-4]`) are `Send` when every component is, a class object's base fields among them; an object held by the type of an `open` or `abstract` class, whose kind the holder cannot see, when the class implements `Send` (`open class Script implements Send:`, `[CLS-4]`; `E7015` otherwise at the line that hands it over: "`s` is a `Script`, an `open` class whose objects may be of any class derived from it, and `Script` does not say any thread may have them; write `pub open class Script implements Send:` (gamekit/src/lib.em line 3), after which every class derived from `Script` is checked for it where it is declared");
edits.why: THR-8's list sentence "class objects are `Send` when every component is" is narrower than its own definition ("nothing reachable from it") for an open class, since the reachable fields are a derived class's. The list now says what the definition says, by the same shape as its own `dyn I` clause.

edits.old: Structural types are `ThreadShared` when every component is.
edits.new: Structural types, and objects of a class that cannot be subclassed, are `ThreadShared` when every component is; an object held by the type of an `open` or `abstract` class when the class implements `ThreadShared` (`[CLS-4]`), and `dyn I` when `I` requires it (`interface I: needs ThreadShared:`), as for `Send` (`[THR-8]`).
edits.why: THR-9 named only structural types: class objects and `dyn I` had no ThreadShared rule at all, so `ref r` of a `Result[int]` given to a scoped task (`ref T` is `Send` when `T` is `ThreadShared`, `[THR-8]`) and an `AnyError` under a `thread_shared` `RwLock` (verdict 165) were undecided. ODR-255 ruled the `dyn` half and the text never said it.

edits.old: a class object is when its fields are;
edits.new: a class object is when its fields are, where its class cannot be subclassed; an object held by the type of an `open` or `abstract` class when the class implements `Send`, and `dyn I` when `I` requires it (`[THR-8]`, `[CLS-4]`);
edits.why: `[TYP-43]` says "the table answers them": the row must give the same answer as THR-8, or the two texts decide one program differently.

edits.old: every component is `ThreadShared` (the `ref A` a value made in a manager's instance holds included, `[TYP-46a]`);
edits.new: every component is `ThreadShared` (the `ref A` a value made in a manager's instance holds included, `[TYP-46a]`); a class object when its fields are, where its class cannot be subclassed; an object held by the type of an `open` or `abstract` class when the class implements `ThreadShared`, and `dyn I` when `I` requires it (`[THR-9]`, `[CLS-4]`);
edits.why: The same for the ThreadShared row, which named neither class objects nor `dyn`.

edits.old:
`ThreadShared` is written only in bounds, `Copy` comes from
  `@derive(Copy)`, and `Sized` is never written: each of these written by hand is `E2040`,
edits.new: `Send` and `ThreadShared` are also written, without `unsafe`, in the `implements` list of an `open` or `abstract` class (`pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`), whose objects' kinds a holder cannot see: there the word is the class family's promise, which the compiler checks against the class's own fields and, where each is declared, against every class derived from it (`[CLS-4]`, `[IFC-3]`, `E2040`), so it vouches for nothing; on a struct, an enum or a class that cannot be subclassed it is refused as below. Otherwise `ThreadShared` is written only in bounds, `Copy` comes from `@derive(Copy)`, and `Sized` is never written: each of these written by hand is `E2040`,
edits.why: TYP-43 allowed a hand-written `Send` only as an `unsafe extend` for a raw pointer, because there the compiler cannot check it. On an open class it can check every member of the family at that member's own line, so the written word is a checked declaration like `interface I: needs Send`, not a vouch; the rule must name the new place or `E3100` would refuse it.

edits.old:
A method pins the class
  that declares it and every class derived from it, whose objects run it; a class pinned both ways,
  by its own methods or with a base's, is `E7015` at the one-thread line
edits.new: A method pins the class that declares it and every class derived from it, whose objects run it; a class pinned both ways, by its own methods or with a base's, or pinned one-thread while it or a base implements `Send` (`[CLS-4]`), is `E7015` at the one-thread line
edits.why: OWN-13 reads a class's kind from its methods and already refuses a class pinned both ways. A method writing `weakref this` or `shares this` in a family that promises `Send` is the same contradiction, and belongs in the same sentence.

edits.new: (ODR-042). An implementation meets its interface's parents for every type it covers: each instance of a generic implementation (`extend[T] PoolFull[T] implements Error:` covers every `T`, so it is `E2040`, the message giving the bounded line, `extend[T: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared)] PoolFull[T] implements Error:`), and each class derived from a class that implements it, whose objects are values of that class (`[TYP-5]` rule 8), checked where the derived class is declared, by the package that declares it, whichever package declares the base (`[BLD-16]`): a parent the base's implementation gives it (`Eq`, `Display`) it has; a marker parent (`Send`, `ThreadShared`, `[CLS-4]`) it meets with its own fields, or is `E2040`, naming the field and the base's line and giving a line that holds a copy of what the field is used for ("`Enemy` is a `Script`, which implements `Send` and `ThreadShared` (gamekit/src/lib.em line 3), so every `Enemy` does too, and `Enemy.level` (line 8) is a `shares Level`, an owner kept on one thread; keep what `Enemy` reads from the level by copy: write `level_name: String` in place of line 8, or share the level between threads: `level: thread_shared Level`").
edits.why: IFC-3 is where the language says what an implementation promises about its interface's parents; it said implementers meet them, not that an implementation meets them for every type it covers. A derived class is covered by its base's implementation (TYP-5 rule 8 upcasts it), so the check for a marker parent falls on the derived class's own fields at its own line, local to the package that can see them. The same sentence closes the generic-instance hole (`PoolFull[T]`) once, for every interface, instead of as a case of `Error`.

edits.old:
interface Error: needs (Debug, Display):
    fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]                            # default: None
edits.new:
interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):   # any thread may have an error
    fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]                            # default: None
edits.why: This is the declaration every bound, every `dyn Error` and every implementer reads ("These are the definitions"); `std/src/core.em` line 80 follows it.

edits.old: (`interface Error: needs (Debug, Display):`)
edits.new: (`interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):`)
edits.why: The generics chapter's example is a second copy of the declaration; left as it was, two texts would decide one program differently.

edits.old:
`Error` is the
  interface of error types: `Display + Debug` with `fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]` (default
  `None`) (§IV.8).
edits.new: `Error` is the interface of error types, `interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):` with `fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]` (default `None`) (§IV.8): any thread may have and read an error, so an error crosses threads by every route a value does (`[THR-2]`), and so do `dyn Error` and `AnyError` (`[THR-8]`, `[THR-9]`, `[ERR-8]`). A type holding a value that stays on one thread (a `shares` or `shares mut` owner, a `weakref T` or `sharedref mut` link, a `Cell`, an object held by the type of an `open` class that does not implement the markers) does not implement `Error`: `E2040` at its `implements Error` (`[IFC-3]`: "`Error` needs `Send` and `ThreadShared`, since any thread may have an error, and `LoadError.script` is a `Script`, an `open` class that does not say any thread may have its objects; write `pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:` (line 3), or keep what the error reports by copy: `entity: int`"), `E2080` at `@derive(Error)`, naming the field (`[DRV-1]`). It may still be a `Result`'s error, matched or printed (`[ERR-1]`, ODR-050).
edits.why: ERR-3 describes the declaration; the two must say one thing. It states one property (any thread may have an error) and leaves the placing of refusals to IFC-3 and DRV-1, and the old `Display + Debug` spelling goes (verdict 110).

edits.old:
An `AnyError` passed through `?` into another
  `AnyError` is handed over (`[ERR-7]`).
edits.new: An `AnyError` passed through `?` into another `AnyError` is handed over (`[ERR-7]`). `AnyError` is `Send` and `ThreadShared` as its parts are: its `owns dyn Error` because `Error` requires both (`[ERR-3]`, `[THR-8]`, `[THR-9]`), its context a list of `String`; so a worker's `Result[int]` comes back through `join`, a channel or a scoped task's result with nothing written (`[THR-10]`, `[THR-15]`, `[THR-11]`), and the one-thread error it cannot carry was refused where that type was declared an error, never at the `?`.
edits.why: The markers of the erased error type were nowhere stated; the gap sweep's program was refused at the spawn with no text saying so. AnyError needs no rule of its own: its markers follow from its fields, which the sentence says.

edits.new: A `pub` class's `implements` list, which the derived classes of other packages were checked against (`[CLS-4]`, `[IFC-3]`), is such a fact too: a reload whose new image removes a marker from it is refused (`E9030`) unless every package whose classes derive from it is rebuilt by the reload, which checks them again; a reload that adds a field to a derived class is checked at that class when the image compiles, before any plan.
edits.why: Annex B compares worked-out facts; the promise a derived class in another package was checked against is a written word of the base, and a reload that takes it away would leave a checked class unchecked. The sentence names the two reload routes the method-4 record found open (a base losing its word, a derived class gaining a field).

edits.old: a one-thread owner in a trampoline class under `threads=any` | `[THR-1]`
edits.new: a one-thread owner in a trampoline class under `threads=any`; a value held by the type of an `open` or `abstract` class that does not implement `Send`, handed to another thread; a method pinning a class one-thread while it or a base implements `Send` | `[CLS-4]`, `[THR-1]`
edits.why: The row lists every refusal that carries the code; THR-8 and OWN-13 now name two more.

edits.old: has no `Display` | `[IFC-6]`, `[TYP-17]`, `[BLD-14]`, `[ERR-4]` |
edits.new: has no `Display`; an implementation that does not meet its interface's parents for every type it covers: a generic implementation (the bounded line given), or a class derived from a class that implements the interface, at its own declaration (`Send` and `ThreadShared` among the parents: a derived class of a class implementing them, or an error type, holding a value that stays on one thread) | `[IFC-6]`, `[TYP-17]`, `[BLD-14]`, `[ERR-4]`, `[IFC-3]`, `[CLS-4]`, `[ERR-3]` |
edits.why: One code, one defining rule: the unmet parent is an unsatisfied bound, which is E2040's meaning; the row says where it now falls.

edits.old: `Send` declared by hand without `unsafe extend`;
edits.new: `Send` declared by hand without `unsafe extend`, other than in an `open` or `abstract` class's `implements` list (`[TYP-43]`);
edits.why: The row would otherwise contradict the edited TYP-43.

designs.refused_program:
# file gamekit/ember.toml
#   [package]
#   name = "gamekit"
#   version = "0.1.0"
#   language = "0.9.20"
#   kind = "lib"
# file gamekit/src/lib.em (line numbers count from its first line)
from std.fmt import Formatter, FmtError

pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:    # line 3: the family's promise
    let entity: int

    pub fn init(entity: int):
        this.entity = entity

pub struct LoadError:
    pub script: Script

extend LoadError implements Display:
    fn fmt(ref mut f: Formatter) -> Result[void, FmtError]:
        return f.write_str("the script could not load")

extend LoadError implements Debug:
    fn fmt_debug(ref mut f: Formatter) -> Result[void, FmtError]:
        return f.write_str("LoadError")

extend LoadError implements Error:                      # line 20: meets Send and ThreadShared, by line 3
    pass

# file game/ember.toml
#   [package]
#   name = "game"
#   version = "0.1.0"
#   language = "0.9.20"
#   [dependencies]
#   gamekit = { path = "../gamekit" }
# file game/src/main.em (line numbers count from its first line)
import std.thread
from gamekit import Script, LoadError

class Level:
    name: String = String("forest")

class Enemy(Script):                                    # line 7
    level: shares Level                                 # line 8

    fn init(entity: int, owns level: shares Level):
        this.level = level
        super.init(entity)

fn make_enemy(entity: int, owns level: shares Level) -> Result[int, LoadError]:
    return Err(LoadError(script=Enemy(entity, owns level)))   # an Enemy, upcast to Script

fn load(entity: int, owns level: shares Level) -> Result[int]:
    return Ok(make_enemy(entity, owns level)?)          # LoadError -> AnyError

fn main():
    level = shares Level()
    r = load(1, shares level)
    h = thread.spawn(owns fn() owns r: r.is_err())
    for i in 0..100000:
        other = shares level
        println(i, other.name.len())
    println(h.join())

# Refused in game's build, at game/src/main.em line 7, with nothing of gamekit compiled again:
#
# error[E2040]: `Enemy` is a `Script`, which implements `Send` and `ThreadShared`
#   (gamekit/src/lib.em line 3), so every `Enemy` does too, and `Enemy.level` (line 8) is a
#   `shares Level`, an owner kept on one thread; keep what `Enemy` reads from the level by copy:
#   write `level_name: String` in place of line 8, or share the level between threads:
#   `level: thread_shared Level`
#
# Had gamekit's line 3 been `pub open class Script:` (no promise), the refusal would instead fall in
# gamekit's own build, at line 20:
#
# error[E2040]: `Error` needs `Send` and `ThreadShared`, since any thread may have an error, and
#   `LoadError.script` is a `Script`, an `open` class that does not say any thread may have its
#   objects; write `pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:` (line 3), or keep what the
#   error reports by copy: `entity: int`
#
# and game's `Enemy`, with its `shares Level`, would compile as any one-thread class does. In neither
# build does the `shares` owner reach the worker thread.
designs.runtime_cost: Nothing. Every judgement here is made when compiling, from a declaration the compiling package sees: the base's `implements` list (in its own text, or in the imported interface file), the derived class's own fields, `Error`'s declared parents. The §X.4 row is the existing "What a function changes, reads and ends; the thread rules; the arena checks | not observable | all checked when compiling (`[EFF-24]`)". No new row (`[COST-5]`). Two existing rows become reachable for an `AnyError` that now crosses, unchanged: "`?` converting an error into `AnyError` | guaranteed present, failure path only | one allocation (`[ERR-11]`)", paid before any hand-over as today; and "An object handed whole to another thread | guaranteed present | ... one load and one test, then a call of the kind's hand-over routine, per owned value whose layout the handing package cannot see (held `dyn I`, of an `open` or `abstract` class, a function value's state)", which the boxed `dyn Error` pays once per `AnyError` handed to another thread, on the failure path only, and which does nothing for a kind whose family carries no weak count. The existing "`@cached` method ... on an object several threads reach, the result is filled once under a once-flag" row now covers a `@cached` method of a class whose objects any thread may have; which classes those are must be read, under `[BLD-16]`, from the class's own declaration (it implements `ThreadShared`, or `Error`), which `[CLS-12]` should say (noted below, not this question's cause). The run-time alternative was priced and turned down: a `Send` flag in the kind's `TypeInfo` tested at each hand-over of a base-typed object would cost one load and one test (the load the hand-over routine already makes), but it can only stop the program, since a `shares` owner inside the object cannot be moved away from its other owners; a compile-time refusal with a line to write would become a stop on the least-tested path, for a conflict between two packages that is nobody's bug at the stopping line (docs/AUTOPILOT.md §4, "A panic has to make sense").
designs.implementer_steps: 1. Parser: nothing; `class_decl` already has `[implements]` ("implements" type {"," type}). Name resolution: accept `Send` and `ThreadShared` in the `implements` list of a class declared `open` or `abstract`; keep `E3100` (Send) and `E2040` (ThreadShared) for the list of a struct, enum or final class, with the message naming the class as one that cannot be subclassed. 2. Marker inference (the function behind `[TYP-43]`'s table), for a class type C: if C is final, infer from its fields, base fields included, as for a struct; if C is `open` or `abstract`, answer from C's declared markers: those in its `implements` list, those in the `implements` lists of its bases, and those among the `needs` of any interface it or a base implements; never from C's fields. For `dyn I`, answer both `Send` and `ThreadShared` from I's `needs` (THR-9's new clause). 3. Class checker, per class D declared in the compiling package (its own source only): collect the interfaces D implements, inherited from bases through their declarations in imported interface files; for each marker among them (direct or via an interface's parents) infer D's own fields' markers, and refuse `E2040` at D's declaration when one fails, naming the field, the base's file and line, and giving the copy line (the field's type with the one-thread word removed, or `String`/`int` for what it reads) and, where it compiles under `[THR-1]`, the `thread_shared` line. Also: if a method of D, or of a base, pins the class one-thread (`[OWN-13]`'s list) while the family implements `Send`, `E7015` at the pinning line. 4. `[IFC-3]` for generic implementations: for `extend[Ps] X[Ps] implements I`, check I's parents hold for `X[Ps]` under the written bounds alone; where one does not, `E2040` giving the line with the bounds added (`[IFC-6]`'s message shape). 5. Hand-over checks (`[THR-2]`, `[THR-10]`, `[THR-15]`, `[THR-1]`, `[THR-11]`): unchanged code paths; they call step 2, so a base-typed value of a class without `implements Send` is `E7015` with the new message naming the class and its declaration line. 6. `std/src/core.em` line 80: `pub interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):`; the IV.8 sketch and TYP-17's example with it. `@derive(Error)` generates its `extend` as today; a field that fails a marker is `E2080` naming the field (DRV-1's existing rule), and a generic type's derive holds per instance as `[STR-5]` already reads every derive. `AnyError` needs no code: its markers follow from `Box[dyn Error]`, `u128` and `Array[String]`. 7. Interface files: no new record. The `implements` list of a `pub` class is already part of its declaration there; `[MOD-9]`'s written-word rule carries it. 8. Hot reload (Annex B): the plan's comparison (`[HR-44]`) adds the `pub` classes' `implements` lists to the facts it compares; a removed marker refuses the reload unless the packages deriving from the class are rebuilt by it; a rebuilt derived class is checked by step 3 when the image compiles. A module loaded at run time (`[ABI-1]`) compiles its derived classes against the base's declaration the same way. 9. FFI: no code; an Ember class extending a C++ class under `threads=creator` (`[FFI-17d]`) is thread-bound (`E7008`), so step 3 refuses `implements Send` on it as on any class whose objects are not `Send`. 10. Tests, each with its break test: the accepted program as a run-pass (two packages, a worker returning `Result[int]`); the refused program as `E2040` at the derived class, and its variant without the promise as `E2040` at the library's `implements Error`; `E7015` at a spawn of a base-typed value of a class without the promise; `E3100` for `implements Send` on a final class; `E7015` for `weakref this` in a `Send` family; `E2040` for `extend[T] PoolFull[T] implements Error:`; a reload test removing `Send` from a `pub open` class with a derived class in another package (`E9030`); `channel[Result[int]]` and a scoped task's `ref r` of a `Result[int]` as run-pass; a `Result[int, DocError]` with `doc: shares Doc`, matched and printed, still compiling (ODR-050).
designs.departs_from_verdict: None. Verdict 61 (the type says whether any thread may run its functions, chosen over the compiler finding it from the whole program): kept and followed; an open class is erased as `fn()` is, and the ruling puts the word on the class. Verdict 86 (the compiler works out what functions do from code): kept; markers of a type were never a body fact, and a final class stays inferred. Verdict 94 (`thread.spawn` takes `thread_shared once fn()`, `R` Send): kept; `AnyError` now meets `R: Send`. Verdict 110 (an interface's parents with `needs`): kept, `interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):`. Verdicts 108, 111, 113 (a `pub` generic and `extend` write their needs): kept; the generic error implementation writes its bound, and the message gives the line. Verdict 164 (a `sharedref mut` link is neither marker): kept; an error holding one is refused at its `implements Error`. Verdict 165 (`thread_shared` refused where the value is made when not ThreadShared): kept; a `thread_shared` holder of `Result[int]`s is now accepted because `AnyError` is `ThreadShared`. Verdict 166 (a scoped task touches no one-thread count): kept. Verdict 23 (a `shares` value never used from two threads): kept, no `shares` owner can be inside an error, a derived class of a `Send` family, or a base-typed value that crosses. Verdict 114 and 101 (hand-over leaves links behind; the 32-byte header): kept; the existing hand-over routine walks the boxed error. ODR-050 (`Result`'s error parameter unbounded): kept; a one-thread error type is still a `Result`'s error, printed by `Display`. ODR-255 (`dyn I` Send/Sync when I requires it): now written for ThreadShared in THR-9. ODR-111 (a lead's ruling, not an owner verdict: `Send` by hand only with `unsafe extend`): touched, not reversed in substance; the new written place is checked by the compiler for every member of the family, so it vouches for nothing, which is why `unsafe` is not written there; reported for the lead.
designs.trade_offs: Given up: (1) A base-typed value of an open class with plain fields and no `implements Send` cannot cross threads, even when the object was made on the line (`s = Script()`); the fix is one line in the class's package, the cost `dyn I` already carries today. (2) Once an open class promises the markers, every class derived from it, in every package, gives up one-thread fields (`shares`, `weakref T`, `sharedref mut`, `Cell`), refused at its own line with a copy line; ordinary hierarchies whose base makes no promise are untouched. (3) An error type cannot hold a one-thread owner, even in a one-thread program (Rust's anyhow `Send + Sync` and Swift's `Error: Sendable` take the same); it may still be a `Result`'s error, matched and printed, and `@derive(Error)` gives the copy line. (4) A hand-written generic error implementation writes `T: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared)`; a derive writes nothing. Kept, against the four goals: C-like speed, nothing runs (the only reachable costs are rows already in the table, on the failure path); Rust-like safety, every check local to a package that can see what it checks, no whole-program fact in any package's code (`[BLD-16]`), the separate-compilation, reload and run-time-module routes all checked at the derived class's own line; Python-like readability, one word on the one thing that crosses threads (the class), nothing on workers, channels, results or `?`; consistency, `dyn I`, `thread_shared fn()` and an open class now decided by one principle (an erased type's markers are declared on it), and `[MOD-9]`'s written-word rule given the word it lacked. The alternatives: inferring the open class's markers from its own fields and making subclasses keep them (option A of the task) costs nothing and is local, but forbids one-thread fields in every subclass of every plain-field base with no way for the base author to decline the promise, which refuses ordinary one-thread games; never-Send-unless-final (option B) is local and free but refuses every polymorphic hand-over and every error holding a base-typed object, with no line to write but "make it final"; the method-4 team's count-every-derived-class puts a whole-program fact in the library's code (`[BLD-16]`) and was shown unsound across a package edge; a recorded "this line relied on Script's Send" (MOD-9a's shape) is local but needs a data-flow record from every relying line to every upcast in every package, far larger than one word; the run-time flag is priced under runtime_cost and can only stop the program.
designs.remaining_doubt: (1) Whether to accept a base-typed value whose exact kind the compiler sees on the line (`s = Script()` handed over at once) without the class's promise: a small flow rule would allow it; left out as not the smallest change, so the `dyn I` cost applies. (2) `[CLS-12]`'s "an object several threads reach" is a whole-program fact as written; under `[BLD-16]` it should be read from the class's declaration (it implements `ThreadShared` or `Error`, or its methods pin it `thread_shared`); that is the method-4 record's S2-2 and an existing gap this ruling only makes reachable, not its cause, so no edit here. (3) Two spellings reach one promise: `implements Send` directly, or `implements Command` with `interface Command: needs Send`; both exist in the grammar today and both are checked by the one IFC-3 sentence, so I kept both rather than refuse one. (4) `Error` requires `ThreadShared` as well as `Send`; `Send` alone would admit an error holding a `Cell`, but then `ref r` to scoped tasks and a `thread_shared` table of results (verdict 165's shape) would be refused; both markers follow Rust's anyhow and Swift. (5) The HR-44 sentence assumes a reload image can rebuild dependant packages or refuse; if Annex B's plan compares only the reloadable package's own facts, the lead may prefer the sentence in `[HR-11]` (the `implements` list as part of a class's schema). (6) The E2040 message's second fix (`level: thread_shared Level`) compiles only where no line then changes the level directly (`[THR-1]`); the message should offer it only then, as the method-4 record's objection E1-2 asked; the message rule in IFC-3 gives the copy line first for that reason.

designs.question: K20: Can AnyError, Result, a channel or a scoped task carry an error type across threads when that error holds an object of an open class another package may derive from? In particular: how are Send and ThreadShared judged for an open or abstract class, and for a value held by that class's type, so that a dependant's subclass (compiled separately, or added by a reload) cannot break a library's judgement ([BLD-16]); then what Error requires and what AnyError's markers are.
designs.summary: An `open` or `abstract` class that another package may derive from says in its own header whether any thread may hold its objects: `open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`. Without the word no value of that class type is `Send` or `ThreadShared`, whatever its fields (its value may be an object of a class the package never sees); with it, the promise binds the class and every class derived from it, checked at each class's own declaration in its own package over all its fields (E7015 at the subclass, naming the field), so a dependant's subclass can never break a library's judgement and an upcast needs no check (the shape of `interface I: needs Send` for `dyn I`, of `[OWN-13]`'s method pinning and of `[OBJ-1]`'s family-wide weak count; an open class no other package can subclass is judged from the derived classes its own package sees, as `[EFF-2a]` already does for its virtual calls). On that footing `Error` requires `Send` and `ThreadShared`, so `dyn Error` and `AnyError` are both, and a worker returns `Result[int]`, a channel carries it and a scoped task reads it with nothing written; an error type holding a one-thread part is `E2040` where it implements `Error`, with a copy line. Nothing runs while the program runs.

edits.rule: TYP-17 (the example of an interface's parents)
edits.old: (`interface Error: needs (Debug, Display):`)
edits.new: (`interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):`)

edits.rule: §IV.8 Standard interfaces, the signature sketch (the definition [ERR-3] cites)
edits.old:
interface Error: needs (Debug, Display):
    fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]                            # default: None
edits.new:
interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):      # any thread may hold and read an error ([ERR-3])

edits.rule: BLD-16 (the list of whole-program facts a package never reads)
edits.old:
not by which of its values are made
  `thread_shared`, not by which of its classes a `weakref` names.
edits.new:
not by which of its values are made
  `thread_shared`, not by which of its classes a `weakref` names, not by which classes a dependant
  derives from one of its `open` or `abstract` classes (`[THR-8]`).

edits.old:
A class is final unless declared `open` or
  `abstract`.
edits.new:
A class is final unless declared `open` or
  `abstract`. An `open` or `abstract` class says in its header whether any thread may hold its
  objects, `implements Send`, `implements ThreadShared`, a promise every class derived from it keeps
  (`[THR-8]`, `[THR-9]`); a final class's markers are read from its fields.

edits.old: a class object is when its fields are;
edits.new: a class object is when its fields are, for a class that is neither `open` nor `abstract`, and when its header writes `implements Send`, for an `open` or `abstract` class, a promise every class derived from it keeps (`[THR-8]`); `dyn I` when `I` requires it;
edits.why: [TYP-43] says the table answers the markers; "a class object is when its fields are" is the narrow reading that let a base-typed value holding a one-thread derived object through, and would contradict the edited [THR-8].

edits.old: every component is `ThreadShared` (the `ref A` a value made in a manager's instance holds included, `[TYP-46a]`);
edits.new: every component is `ThreadShared` (the `ref A` a value made in a manager's instance holds included, `[TYP-46a]`); a class object as for `Send`: by its fields for a class that is neither `open` nor `abstract`, by `implements ThreadShared` in its header for an `open` or `abstract` class (`[THR-8]`); `dyn I` when `I` requires it (`[THR-9]`);

edits.old: Structural types are `ThreadShared` when every component is.
edits.new:
Structural types, and objects of a class that is neither `open` nor `abstract`, are `ThreadShared`
  when every component is; an object of an `open` or `abstract` class only when its header writes
  `implements ThreadShared`, a promise every class derived from it keeps, checked at each class's
  declaration (`[THR-8]`); `dyn I` when `I` requires it (`interface I: needs (Send, ThreadShared):`,

edits.why: [THR-9] had the same gap as [THR-8] for class objects and no words for a `dyn` at all; ODR-255 ruled the `dyn` half and the text never said it. `AnyError`'s `ThreadShared` rests on this clause.

edits.old: A derive whose requirement a field does not meet is `E2080`, naming the field.
edits.new:
A derive whose requirement a field does not meet is `E2080`, naming the field (`@derive(Error)` on a
  type with a `shares` field: `Error` needs `Send`, `[ERR-3]`). On a generic type the generated
  `extend` writes, as its parameters' needs, what its fields need of them (`@derive(Error)` on `[T]`
  above `enum SpawnError:` with `Rejected(T)` generates `extend[T: needs (Debug, Send, ThreadShared)]
  SpawnError[T] implements Error:`), so the derive holds for the instances that meet them, as
  `@derive(Copy)` on `[T]` above `pub struct Range:` is `Copy` when `T` is (ODR-027, `[IFC-3]`).

edits.old:
A field's type schema includes the words its type is
  written with (`owns`, `shares`, `shares mut`, `thread_shared`, `weakref`, `sharedref mut`, `ref`,
  `ref mut`, `using A`), so a change of one is a change of the field's type.
edits.new:
A field's type schema includes the words its type is
  written with (`owns`, `shares`, `shares mut`, `thread_shared`, `weakref`, `sharedref mut`, `ref`,
  `ref mut`, `using A`), so a change of one is a change of the field's type. A class's schema
  includes the promise its header writes (`implements Send`, `implements ThreadShared`, `[THR-8]`): a
  new image that drops one from a class is refused in plan (`E9030`) while code the reload does not
  rebuild, another package's or a frame below a checkpoint, was checked against it, as `[HR-44]`
  refuses a changed fact; a derived class rebuilt with a field that breaks a promise is refused where
  it compiles, before any plan.
edits.why: Hot reload is a route to the same race: a reload that adds a `shares` field to a derived class, or removes the base's promise, must meet the same check. The added field is refused by the rebuilt package's own compile; the dropped promise is a schema change that plan compares, so nothing runs for it.

edits.old: `unwrap` or `expect` on a `Result` whose error type has no `Display` | `[IFC-6]`, `[TYP-17]`, `[BLD-14]`, `[ERR-4]` |
edits.new: `unwrap` or `expect` on a `Result` whose error type has no `Display`; an implementation that does not meet its interface's parents for every type it covers (a field that is not `Send` in a type implementing `Error`; a generic implementation without the needs its parents put on its parameters), at the implementation; `implements Send` or `implements ThreadShared` on a struct, an enum or a class that cannot be subclassed | `[IFC-6]`, `[TYP-17]`, `[BLD-14]`, `[ERR-4]`, `[IFC-3]`, `[ERR-3]`, `[TYP-43]` |

edits.old: a `thread_shared` object of a class pinned to one thread or with a `weakref T` field;
edits.new: a `thread_shared` object of a class pinned to one thread or with a `weakref T` field; a field that is not `Send` or `ThreadShared` in an `open` or `abstract` class whose header promises it, or in a class derived from one that does, at the class; a value of an `open` or `abstract` class type with no such promise reaching another thread, `thread_shared` on a new object of such a class included;
edits.why: The registry row names every refusal under the code; [THR-8] is already among its rules.

edits.old:
`ThreadShared` is written only in bounds, `Copy` comes from
  `@derive(Copy)`, and `Sized` is never written: each of these written by hand is `E2040`, as is an
  `unsafe extend` of any interface but `Send` or an `unsafe interface` (ODR-111).
edits.new:
`ThreadShared` is written only in bounds, `Copy` comes from
  `@derive(Copy)`, and `Sized` is never written: each of these written by hand is `E2040`, as is an
  `unsafe extend` of any interface but `Send` or an `unsafe interface` (ODR-111); the one other place
  `Send` and `ThreadShared` are written is the header of an `open` or `abstract` class (`open class
  Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`), where each is a promise for every class of the family that
  the compiler checks at each class's declaration (`[THR-8]`), so it needs no `unsafe`; on a struct,
  an enum or a class that is neither `open` nor `abstract`, whose markers are inferred, it is `E2040`
  ("`Door` cannot be subclassed, so its `Send` is read from its fields; remove `implements Send`").
edits.why: [TYP-43] refused every hand-written marker but the `unsafe extend` vouch; the header promise is a bound the compiler checks, as `interface I: needs Send` is, not a vouch, so it is allowed without `unsafe` and refused where inference already answers. The grammar's `class_decl` already parses `implements Send`; no grammar change.

edits.old:
`interface Ord: needs Eq` requires implementers of `Ord` to
  implement `Eq`.
edits.new:
`interface Ord: needs Eq` requires implementers of `Ord` to
  implement `Eq`: an implementation meets its interface's parents for every type it covers, checked
  where it is written (`E2040`, naming the part that does not and giving the line that compiles). A
  generic implementation covers every instance its brackets allow, so it writes the needs the parents
  put on its parameters (`extend[T: needs (Send, ThreadShared)] PoolFull[T] implements Error:`;
  `extend[T] PoolFull[T] implements Error:` is `E2040` with that line, since a declaration means what
  it says, verdict 132), as a `pub` generic function writes its bounds (`[IFC-6]`). An `open` or
  `abstract` class meets a marker parent through the promise in its header, which every class derived
  from it keeps (`[THR-8]`), so a derived class in another package is checked at its own declaration
  and the implementation is never checked again.
edits.why: [IFC-3] said implementers meet the parents but not that an implementation meets them for every type it covers; a generic error implementation over an unbounded `T` would put `PoolFull[shares Enemy]` into an `AnyError`. Stated once for every interface with parents (`Ord`, `IndexMut`, a program's `Command: needs Send`), never as a case of `Error`.

edits.new:
`AnyError` is `Send` and `ThreadShared`: its `owns dyn Error` is, since `Error` requires both
  (`[THR-8]`, `[THR-9]`), and its context chain is text. So a worker returns `Result[int]` (`R` is
  `Send`, `[THR-10]`, `[THR-11]`), a channel carries one (`[THR-15]`), a `thread_shared` holder keeps
  one under its lock (`[THR-1]`) and a scoped task reads one through `ref`. Nothing is checked at `?`:
  every `E: needs Error` met the requirement where it implemented `Error`, in its own package, and an
  `AnyError` handed to another thread walks the error it holds by that error's own hand-over routine
  (`[THR-2]`), as any `owns dyn I` value is walked.
edits.why: The question's missing words: the erased error's markers, stated by what it may hold. `From[E]` for every `E: needs Error` stays true as written, and the `?` line stays free of any check.

edits.old:
`Error` is the
  interface of error types: `Display + Debug` with `fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]` (default

edits.new:
`Error` is the
  interface of error types, `interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):` with
  `fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]` (default `None`) (§IV.8): any thread may hold and read an
  error, so `dyn Error`, and every `Result` whose error is one, goes to a worker thread, through a
  channel and into a scoped task's view as any `Send` and `ThreadShared` value does (`[THR-8]`,

  `Cell`, an object of an `open` class whose header makes no promise, `[THR-8]`) is not an error:
  where it implements `Error` it is `E2040`, naming the field and giving the line that compiles
  (`[IFC-3]`; "`LoadError.script` is a `Script`, an `open` class whose header does not say that any
  thread may hold its objects, so a `LoadError` may hold an object of a class another package derives
  from `Script`, and `Error` needs `Send` and `ThreadShared`; write `pub open class Script implements

edits.why: [ERR-3] describes the declaration of §IV.8 and must say the same thing; the `Display + Debug` spelling goes (verdict 110). It states one property, any thread may hold an error, and leaves the cases to [THR-8], [IFC-3] and [DRV-1].

edits.rule: THR-8 (the cause: the class-object clause of the `Send` list)
edits.old:
Structs, enums, tuples, fixed arrays, collections and class objects
  are `Send` when every component is; an `owns T` when `T` is; `ref T` and `Span[T]` when `T` is

Structs, enums, tuples, fixed arrays, collections and objects of a class that is
  neither `open` nor `abstract` are `Send` when every component is; an `owns T` when `T` is; `ref T`
  and `Span[T]` when `T` is `ThreadShared`, `ref mut T` and `MutSpan[T]` when `T` is `Send`; a
  `thread_shared T`, and a `weakref thread_shared T`, when `T` is `Send` and `ThreadShared`; `dyn I`
  when `I` requires it (`interface I: needs Send:`). **An `open` or `abstract` class says in its

  any class derived from it, in a package the class's package never sees (`[TYP-5]` rule 8,
  `[BLD-16]`), so its own fields decide nothing for the type: it is `Send` only when its header
  writes `implements Send`, and `ThreadShared` only when it writes `implements ThreadShared` (`open
  class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`), a promise for the class and every class derived from
  it, as a method pins a class and its derived classes (`[OWN-13]`) and a weak count is carried by a

  else: a field that is not `Send`, or not `ThreadShared`, where the class or a base promises it is
  `E7015` at the class, naming the field and the promise ("`Enemy.level` is a `shares Level` owner,
  which stays on one thread, and `Script` promises that any thread may hold its objects (`pub open
  class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`, gamekit/src/lib.em line 3), a promise every class
  derived from it keeps; keep what the enemy needs as a copy, `level_name: String`, or share the
  level between threads, `level: thread_shared Level`, changed only through its own operations
  (`[THR-1]`)"). A derived class may write a promise its base does not; it holds for it and its
  derived classes, never for the base. On a generic class the promise holds for each instance whose

  the promise from the declaration it imports (`[MOD-9]`: a word exists, so only the written word

  subclassed outside its package (`[EFF-2a]`) needs no promise: its markers are read from the fields
  of every class its package derives from it, as a call through its `virtual` methods counts every
  override the package has (`[EFF-2a]`, `[CLS-2]`), and a refusal names the derived class and its
  field. A value of a class type whose header makes no promise it needs, reaching another thread by
  any route of `[THR-2]`, `thread_shared Script()` included (`[THR-1]`), is `E7015` at that line,
  whose message gives the promise line, or the value held by a class that cannot be subclassed

  objects, so it may be an object of a class another package derives from `Script`; write `pub open

edits.why: This is the cause. "class objects are `Send` when every component is" counts the declared class's fields, narrower than [THR-8]'s own definition ("nothing reachable from it"), and for an `open` class the components are a whole-program fact [BLD-16] forbids a package to read. Making the family's markers a word of the root's declaration, checked at every class's own line, is the one shape that is local to each package, needs no check at an upcast or a hand-over, and refuses the one-thread field at the class that holds it. It is the shape the text already uses for `dyn I` (`needs Send`), for a class's kind ([OWN-13]) and for the weak count ([OBJ-1]), and the owner chose it for function types over a whole-program search (verdict 61).

# The same library, and a game whose subclass keeps the promise. Nothing thread-related is written in the
# game: the default error type comes back from a worker thread.

# file gamekit/src/lib.em  (package gamekit, kind = "lib", as in the refused program)
from std.fmt import Formatter, FmtError

pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:
    pub entity: int

    pub fn init(entity: int):
        this.entity = entity

pub struct LoadError:
    pub script: Script

extend LoadError implements Display:
    fn fmt(ref mut f: Formatter) -> Result[void, FmtError]:
        return f.write_str(f"script {this.script.entity} could not load")

extend LoadError implements Debug:
    fn fmt_debug(ref mut f: Formatter) -> Result[void, FmtError]:

extend LoadError implements Error:
    pass

pub fn fail(owns s: Script) -> Result[int, LoadError]:

# file game/src/main.em  (package game, depends on gamekit)
import std.fs
import std.thread
from gamekit import Script, fail

class Door(Script):                     # checked here: `name` is Send and ThreadShared, the promise holds
    name: String = String("gate")

fn load(path: StrView) -> Result[int]:  # fails with any error: AnyError
    text = fs.read_to_string(path)?     # io.Error -> AnyError
    return Ok(text.len())

fn tick(owns s: Script) -> Result[int]:
    return Ok(fail(owns s)?)            # LoadError -> AnyError; the error carries a Door

fn main() -> Result[void]:
    h = thread.spawn(owns fn() => load("level1.cfg"))   # R = Result[int, AnyError], Send ([THR-10])
    g = thread.spawn(owns fn() => tick(owns Door(7)))   # a Script that is a Door crosses inside an AnyError
    n = h.join()?                                        # the worker's error, if any, is main's
    println(n)
    match g.join():
        Ok(_) => println("loaded")
        Err(e) => println(e)                             # prints: script 7 could not load
    return Ok(())
# Prints the file's length and `script 7 could not load`, or `error: <the system's message>` with status 1
# when level1.cfg is missing. Every hand-over of an AnyError is one move; the Door's weak-count compare at
# the hand-over goes through LoadError's own hand-over routine ([THR-2]), as for any `owns dyn I` value.
designs.runtime_cost: Nothing new. `Send` and `ThreadShared` are inferred and checked when compiling; the promise is a header word read from the class's declaration (in its package, or in its interface file), and each class of a family is checked once, at its declaration, over the marker properties every type already has (`[TYP-1]`). No check at an upcast, at `?`, at a spawn, at a send or at a join. What runs is already in §X.4: the `[COST-3]` row "An object handed whole to another thread" ("one load and one test, then a call of the kind's hand-over routine, per owned value whose layout the handing package cannot see (held `dyn I`, of an `open` or `abstract` class, a function value's state)"), which an `AnyError` handed to another thread pays for its boxed error exactly as any `owns dyn I` value does today, and `[ERR-11]`'s one allocation on the failure path, unchanged. The row "No data race | always, via `Send`, `ThreadShared` and the thread rules (Part XI) | never | type system; zero cost" stays true. No new §X.4 row.
designs.implementer_steps:
1. Parser: nothing. `class_decl := ["open" | "abstract"] "class" IDENT ["(" type ")"] [implements] ...` with `implements := "implements" type {"," type}` already parses `implements Send, ThreadShared`.
2. Class declaration check (the package that declares the class): collect the family's promises = the markers named in this header's `implements` list that are `Send` or `ThreadShared` (resolved to `std.core`'s interfaces by identity, never by name, `[TYP-43]`) plus the base's promises (from the base's declaration in source, or from its interface file for an imported base). On a struct, enum or final class a listed marker is E2040 (remove it). For each promised marker, fold the marker property over every field, inherited fields included; the first field lacking it is E7015 at the class with the message of `[THR-8]` (the promise's line and package, a copy line, and `thread_shared` only where `[THR-1]`'s no-direct-change rule can then hold). A generic class checks with its parameters' written needs.
3. Marker inference `is_send(T)` / `is_thread_shared(T)`: a class type `C` that is final: fold over fields (as today). `C` `open` or `abstract` and subclassable outside its package (`pub`): the promise set holds the marker. `C` `open` or `abstract` and not subclassable outside its package: fold over the fields of every class the package derives from it (the same closed set `[EFF-2a]`/`[CLS-2]` use for its overrides). `dyn I`: `I`'s needs for both markers. Everything else unchanged. Cache per type as the other properties of `[TYP-1]` are.
4. Interface files (`[MOD-9]`): a `pub` class's header, promises included, is already exported as the written declaration; make sure a dependant reading the base from the interface file gets the promise set and the base's own-field markers (needed for a derived class that adds a promise its base lacks). Reload manifest (`[HR-8]`, `[HR-11]`): the schema hash of a class includes its promise set; plan refuses E9030 when an image drops a promise a non-rebuilt package or a live frame was checked against.
5. Interface implementations (`[IFC-3]`): at every `extend X implements I:` and `class X implements I:`, for each parent `P` of `I` (transitively), check `X: P` with the implementation's written bounds; unmet → E2040 at the implementation, naming the field (concrete) or giving the bounded `extend` line (generic). `@derive(…)` on a generic type generates the `extend` with the needs its fields require (`[DRV-1]`), then runs the same check.
6. `std.core`: `pub interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):` (core.em line 80); `AnyError` (core.em line 92) then infers both markers from `owns dyn Error` and its text chain. Compile std once under the new check: every std error type holds codes and text and passes; `pub open class AnyStorage` (std/src/ecs.em line 101) writes `implements Send, ThreadShared` if `World`s cross threads (ODR-218's `run_parallel`), else nothing.
7. Diagnostics: E7015 at the class (new message), E2040 at the implementation (new message), the existing E7015 for a promise-less open-class value reaching another thread with the promise line; all follow verdict 73 (the given line compiles: the copy line always does).
8. Tests (`[TST-4a]`, one accept and one reject per code): the two-package refused program above (E7015 at the subclass; E2040 at the library's `extend` without the promise); the accepted program (a worker returning `Result[int]`, a `Sender[Result[int]]`, a `ref` of a `Result[int]` in a scoped task, an `AnyError` under a `thread_shared` holder's lock); a private open hierarchy crossing threads with nothing written (accept) and the same with a one-thread subclass (E7015 naming the subclass); `implements Send` on a final class (E2040); a generic `extend[T] X[T] implements Error` (E2040 with the bounded line) and the bounded form (accept); a reload that adds a `shares` field to a subclass of a promised family (refused at compile) and one that drops a promise (E9030 in plan); the `[ERR-12]` path: a one-thread type as a `Result`'s error printed by `main` (accept).
designs.departs_from_verdict: None. Verdicts touched and kept: 61 (a type says which threads may hold its values, chosen over a whole-program search: extended from function types to open classes, the header word); 94 (`thread.spawn` takes a `thread_shared fn()` and `R` MUST be `Send`: unchanged, now met by `AnyError`); 110 (parents written with `needs`: `interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):`); 108, 111, 113 (a `pub` generic and an `extend` write their needs: a generic implementation of `Error` writes `T: needs (Send, ThreadShared)`); 132 (a declaration means what it says: `extend[T] X[T] implements Error:` is refused, never quietly narrowed); 73 (the given fix compiles: a copy line is always offered); 86 and 122 (facts worked out from bodies: untouched, markers come from declarations); 164, 165, 166 (a `sharedref mut`, a non-`ThreadShared` part, a scoped task's counts: each error type holding one is refused where it implements `Error`; a derived class holding one is refused at its declaration); 23 (a `shares` value never used from two threads: none can sit inside an error, a derived class of a promised family, or a base-typed value that crosses); 114 (a handed object's links say gone: `[THR-2]`'s compare reaches the boxed error through its hand-over routine, already in the text); 106 (contracts on function types: untouched). Delegated rulings touched: ODR-255 (its `ThreadShared` half is now written in `[THR-9]`); ODR-111 (`Send` by hand only as `unsafe extend`: kept for the vouch; the class-header promise is a compiler-checked bound, not a vouch, and `[TYP-43]` says so); ODR-050 (a `Result`'s error parameter is unbounded: kept, a one-thread type stays a `Result` error printed by `main`). The owner gave no verdict on K20 itself (J6-16 was routed to him); this ruling is for him, with option A's cost stated: an error type holding a one-thread part is refused where it implements `Error`, even in a one-thread program, the fix being a copy.
designs.trade_offs: Safety (never compromised): no program is accepted that breaks a promise. Every class of a family is checked in the package that declares it, from a word in a declaration that package sees, so separate compilation, a library update and a reload cannot slip a one-thread field under a `Send` judgement; the erased routes (`dyn Error`, `AnyError`, `Result[T]`, channels, scoped views, `thread_shared` holders) all rest on `Error`'s requirement, which every implementer met locally; the FFI's `threads(any)` callbacks and `threads=any` trampolines read the same markers. Against option (a) of the question (an open class's markers are its own fields, and every subclass must keep them, with no word): safe, but it would force `Send` on every subclass of every library base whose fields happen to be plain (`Script`, `Node`, `Widget`), refusing the ordinary one-thread game that gives `Enemy(Script)` a `shares Level` or a `weakref Player`; the author of the base never chose that. Against option (b) (a base-typed value is never `Send` unless the class is final, Swift's rule for `Sendable` classes): safe, but no open hierarchy could ever cross threads or be read by scoped tasks (std's own `AnyStorage` family included), and the owner's condition forbids dropping a feature to get past a check. The chosen rule is (b)'s default with (a)'s discipline opted into by one word on the class header, so a one-thread subclass is refused only where the base's author promised threads, and an open class private to its package needs no word at all. What is given up: a `pub open` class's objects cross threads only when its author writes `implements Send` (and `ThreadShared` for shared reads), one word on the thing it describes; a dependant cannot add a one-thread field to a class of a promised family (the message gives a copy); an error type holding a one-thread part, or an object of a promise-less open class, is not an `Error` (it is `E2040` at its `implements Error`, even in a program with one thread), though it stays a `Result` error whose `Display` `main` prints; `Error` requiring `ThreadShared` as well as `Send` refuses an error holding a `Cell` or a `ref mut`, rare, so that `ref AnyError` reaches a scoped task and an `AnyError` sits under a `thread_shared` holder's lock, as Rust's `anyhow` requires `Send + Sync`. Speed: nothing runs; every check is at a declaration; `AnyError` keeps its layout and its one allocation on the failure path. Readability: the worker loses an import, a concrete error type and an error enum; ordinary code writes nothing; the word appears only where threads hold a family, and reads as what it means. Consistency: the same shape as `interface I: needs Send` for `dyn I`, `[OWN-13]`'s pinning of a family by a method, `[OBJ-1]`'s family-wide weak count decided by the root's package, `[EFF-2a]`'s "a class that cannot be subclassed outside its package", `[MOD-9]`'s "where a word exists, only the written word counts across the edge", and `[BLD-16]`. Research used as input: Swift makes a `Sendable` class `final` because a subclass may add non-`Sendable` state; Ember can allow a non-final family because every subclass is compiled by Ember with the check; Rust's `anyhow::Error` requires `Send + Sync`, and `Box<dyn Error>` carries the markers only when written after `dyn`; C++'s `std::exception_ptr` crosses threads with no check at all.
designs.remaining_doubt: 1. Syntax: the promise is written as `implements Send, ThreadShared` because `class_decl` already parses it and it reads as what it means for every object of the family; the owner may prefer an interface-style `needs` clause on the class header (verdict 110's spelling), which would need a grammar change. 2. Whether `Error` should require `ThreadShared` as well as `Send`: `Send` alone serves `thread.spawn`, channels and joins; `ThreadShared` is needed only for `ref AnyError` in a scoped task and an `AnyError` under a `thread_shared` holder's lock; both chosen, as the method-4 team and Rust's `anyhow` do, at the cost of refusing an error holding a `Cell` as an `Error`. 3. std must be compiled once under the new check: every std error type is expected to pass (codes and text), and `pub open class AnyStorage` (std/src/ecs.em line 101) needs the promise if a `World` is meant to cross threads (ODR-218); that is a std edit for the hardening, not a spec gap, but it was not verified here (read only). 4. The reload sentence is placed in `[HR-11]` (the schema) rather than `[HR-44]` (worked-out facts), since the promise is a written word; the lead may prefer it in `[HR-44]`. 5. `thread_shared Script()` for a promise-less `pub open` class is stated as `E7015` at the making line in `[THR-8]`'s edit, reading `[THR-1]`'s "everything reachable from it is `Send`" to include the value itself; without that sentence an implementer could read `[THR-1]` as fields only and let a `thread_shared Script` exist that can never leave its thread, harmless but confusing. 6. For an `open` class private to its package, the markers are read from every derived class the package declares, a package-wide fact `[BLD-16]` allows and `[EFF-2a]` already uses for overrides; a lead who wants one rule only can drop that sentence and require the word on every `open` class at the cost of one word in such programs. 7. The library-side refusal (E2040 at `extend LoadError implements Error:` without the promise) means a library update that drops a promise is an interface change a dependant's compile reports with the chain (`[DIA-27]`); the spec says this generally for interface changes, and no words were added for it here.

designs.question: K20 (J6-16): Can AnyError, Result, a channel or a scoped task carry an error type across threads when that error holds an object of an open class another package may derive from? In particular: how are Send and ThreadShared judged for an open class and for a value holding one, so that a dependant's subclass cannot break a library's judgement without any whole-program fact ([BLD-16]); and what are Error's requirements and AnyError's markers?
designs.summary: The rule a newcomer holds: an error is plain data any thread may hold (`interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared)`), so `AnyError` and every `dyn Error` are `Send` and `ThreadShared` and a worker returns `Result[int]` with nothing written; and a base class whose objects may travel between threads says so in its header (`pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`), which every subclass is then held to where it is declared. An object held by a `pub` `open` or `abstract` class type is otherwise neither `Send` nor `ThreadShared`, because the package judging it never sees the classes a dependant derives ([BLD-16]); an `open` class no other package can subclass is judged from its own package's derived classes with nothing written, as [EFF-2a] already does for virtual calls; and a `thread_shared T` of an open `T` is `Send` and `ThreadShared` because its making line checked the object's own class (verdict 165). The method-4 hole closes at the library's own line (`extend LoadError implements Error:` is `E2040` while `Script` promises nothing) and, once the base promises, at the game's own line (`class Enemy(Script):` holding `shares Level` is `E7015`), never at a spawn far away.

# file gamekit/ember.toml
#   [package]
#   name = "gamekit"
#   version = "0.1.0"
#   language = "0.9.20"
#   kind = "lib"
# file gamekit/src/lib.em
from std.fmt import Formatter, FmtError

pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:   # a promise every derived class is checked against
    pub entity: int

    pub fn init(entity: int):
        this.entity = entity

    pub virtual fn on_update(dt: f32):
        pass

pub struct LoadError:
    pub script: Script

extend LoadError implements Display:
    fn fmt(ref mut f: Formatter) -> Result[void, FmtError]:
        return f.write_str(f"script {this.script.entity} could not load")

extend LoadError implements Debug:
    fn fmt_debug(ref mut f: Formatter) -> Result[void, FmtError]:
        return f.write_str("LoadError")

extend LoadError implements Error:                     # Send and ThreadShared: Script promises both
    pass

pub fn attach(owns s: Script, ok: bool) -> Result[int, LoadError]:
    if ok:
        return Ok(s.entity)
    return Err(LoadError(script=s))
