import std.fs
import std.thread
from gamekit import Script, attach

class Door(Script):                                    # plain fields: meets Script's promise, nothing written
    angle: f32 = 0.0

    override fn on_update(dt: f32):
        this.angle = min(this.angle + 90.0 * dt, 90.0)

fn load(path: StrView) -> Result[int]:                 # fails with any error: AnyError
    text = fs.read_to_string(path)?                    # io.Error -> AnyError
    n = attach(owns Door(7), text.len() > 0)?          # LoadError (holding a Door as a Script) -> AnyError
    return Ok(text.len() + n)

fn main() -> Result[void]:
    h = thread.spawn(owns fn() => load("level1.cfg"))  # R = Result[int, AnyError], Send: accepted
    n = h.join()?                                      # the error, if any, ends on this thread
    println(n)
    return Ok(())

# Prints the file's length plus 7, or `error: script 7 could not load` (status 1), or the system's message
# for a missing file. Nothing is written about threads in game; the only word is gamekit's promise.
designs.runtime_cost: Nothing new. Every judgement here (an open class's promise, each derived class against it, `Error`'s parents, `dyn Error`'s markers) is made when compiling. What runs is already in §X.4: the row "`?` converting an error into `AnyError` | guaranteed present, failure path only | one allocation (`[ERR-11]`)", unchanged; and the row "An object handed whole to another thread", whose words "one load and one test, then a call of the kind's hand-over routine, per owned value whose layout the handing package cannot see (held `dyn I`, of an `open` or `abstract` class, ...)" already price the `Err` path of a handed `Result[int]` (its `owns dyn Error`) and a handed base-class object, with "nothing for a value whose type can own no such object". A `@cached` method of a class that implements `Error` falls under the existing clause of the `@cached` row, "on an object several threads reach, the result is filled once under a once-flag", since such objects may now be read by several threads; that clause existed for every `ThreadShared` class. No new row ([COST-5]).
designs.implementer_steps:
1. std.core: change `pub interface Error: needs (Debug, Display):` (std/src/core.em line 80) to `needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared)`. Check std's own error types against it: `io.Error`, `ParseError` (std/src/string.em 25), `CppError` (std/src/ffi.em 149), the two `@derive(Error)` enums in core.em (222, 228) hold plain data; `SendError[T]` (std/src/sync.em 122) gets its `Error` implementation under `[T: needs (Send, ThreadShared)]`. `AnyError`'s markers then follow by inference from `owns dyn Error` plus its text chain; write nothing on it.
2. The marker judge (the function that decides `Send`/`ThreadShared` for a type) gains the class case: (a) class neither `open` nor `abstract`: its fields, plus the one-thread pin from its methods ([OWN-13], [BLD-14] item 8) which makes it neither; (b) `open`/`abstract` and `pub` (another package may subclass it): read the class family's promises, collected along the base chain from each class's header `implements` list and the `extend ... implements` blocks of its own package (coherence, [TYP-20]), an interface's `needs` expanded transitively (`Error` gives `Send` and `ThreadShared`), and `threads=any` on a trampoline class; the marker holds iff promised; (c) `open`/`abstract` and not `pub`: the fields and pins of the class and of every class in this package deriving from it, transitively (the same walk [EFF-2a] makes for a non-`pub` class's virtual calls). (d) `thread_shared T`, `weakref thread_shared T` with `T` in case (b) or (c): `Send` and `ThreadShared` unconditionally. (e) `dyn I`: `ThreadShared` iff `I` requires it, beside the existing `Send` test.
3. At every class declaration `class D(B):`, after fields are resolved: compute B's family promises as in 2(b) (B's own package by its source, another package by its interface file); for each promised marker, judge D's own fields as a struct of those fields (D's own methods' pin included) and report `E7015` at the field (or the pinning method line), with the message naming the base's promise line, the field and the two lines (a `thread_shared` field, or a copy). Record D's resulting promises (the family's) in the interface file as part of [BLD-14] item 8.
4. At `implements I` (header or `extend`), for each marker parent of `I` (transitively), judge the implementing type with the extend's bounds in force (a type parameter has exactly the markers its `needs` list gives); failure is `E2040` with the bounded `extend` line (collect the needed markers per parameter that reaches a field). For `@derive(Error)` (and every derive) on a generic type, generate the `extend` with per-parameter needs collected the same way; the expanded text is what `ember inspect --expand` prints.
5. Interface file: a `pub open`/`abstract` class's header `implements` list and its package's `extend ... implements Send/ThreadShared` blocks are already written words and already exported; make sure the exporter does not drop a memberless `extend`, and that the reader resolves `implements Error` to its marker parents through the interface's recorded `needs`.
6. Hot reload: add the family's promises to an `open`/`abstract` class's schema ([HR-11]'s "kind, base, layout attributes"); Plan compares old and new and refuses (`E9030`) a change unless every package in the loaded set that derives from the class is in the image being reloaded (those are recompiled and so re-run step 3).
7. Diagnostics: add the `E7015`, `E2040` and `E3100` row texts; `Send`/`ThreadShared` in a class header on a class that is neither `open` nor `abstract`, or on a struct or enum, keeps today's refusals (`E3100`, `E2040`).
8. Nothing changes in codegen: no new TypeInfo field, no new header bit, no new runtime call; THR-2's hand-over routine for a `dyn` or open-class value already exists.
9. Tests: the refused program above (`E7015` at game, `E2040` at gamekit without the promise), the accepted program (prints the length), `extend[T] PoolFull[T] implements Error:` (`E2040` with the bounded line), a non-`pub` open class with a `shares`-holding subclass handed to `thread.spawn` (`E7015` naming the subclass's field, nothing written), `thread_shared Script` of a promising-nothing `pub open class Script` handed to a thread (accepted), and a reload that adds the promise without rebuilding the deriving package (`E9030`).
designs.departs_from_verdict: None of the owner's. Verdict 61 (the type says which threads may run or have it, over a whole-program search): kept and extended, the class header says it. Verdict 94 (`thread.spawn` takes `thread_shared once fn() -> R`, `R` `Send`): kept, `spawn`'s line is unchanged and `Result[int]` now meets it. Verdict 110 (parents with `needs`): kept, the three copies of `Error`'s declaration use it. Verdicts 108, 111, 113 (a `pub` generic and an `extend` write their needs; the compiler gives the whole line): kept, the generic error implementation writes `[T: needs (Send, ThreadShared)]` and the message gives it. Verdict 132 (a declaration means what it says): kept, no implementation quietly holds for some arguments. Verdicts 164, 165, 166 and 23: kept; 165 is relied on for `thread_shared T` of an open `T`. Verdict 114 (a handed object's links say gone): kept, THR-2's routine already walks a `dyn` value. Verdicts 86 and 122 (what a call changes is worked out from every function the program can put there): untouched; a marker is a property of a type, decided per BLD-16 (lead ruling N76), not a call's effect. ODR-050 (a `Result`'s error is unbounded) and ODR-255 (`dyn I` is Send/Sync when `I` requires it) kept, the latter's `ThreadShared` half now written. The ruling departs from two non-verdicts: the method-4 team's decision 3 option (i) (count every derived class the program declares), which [BLD-16] now forbids and whose hole S2-1/E2-1 blocked that design, and the gap sweep's recommended option A (check at the `?`), which puts three marker words on every generic function that uses `?` into `AnyError`.
designs.trade_offs: Given up: (1) An error type holding a one-thread value (a `shares` owner, a `Cell`, a `weakref T` link, an undeclared base-class object) is not an `Error`, even in a program with one thread; it remains a `Result`'s error printed by `Display`, but does not pass through `?` into `AnyError` or stand behind `dyn Error`. The fix is to hold a copy of what the error reports, which is what an error is. Swift refuses the same type at its declaration; Rust's `anyhow` refuses it at the `?`. (2) A library whose error keeps the failing base-class object must either keep a copy of what it reports or make the base promise `Send, ThreadShared`, and that promise forbids every subclass in every dependant a `shares` field, a `Cell`, a `weakref T` link or `weakref this`; an engine that wants one-thread scripts keeps plain data in its errors. (3) An object held by a `pub` `open` or `abstract` class type that promises nothing is handed to no thread, read by no scoped task through `ref`, and sent through no channel, even in a program whose every subclass is plain: the judging package cannot see the subclasses, and the readable alternative is one written promise rather than a fact of the whole program ([BLD-16]). `thread_shared Script` is the second route, checked at each making line. (4) `SendError[T]` is an `Error` only for a `ThreadShared` `T`, so `tx.send(owns cell)?` into `AnyError` on a channel of `Cell[int]` is refused (Rust's `anyhow` has the same edge). (5) A reload that changes a base's promise must rebuild every package deriving from it. (6) One more thing a reader learns: `pub open` classes are judged by their promise, other classes by their fields; the same split [EFF-2a] already draws for virtual calls, so it is one rule twice, not two rules. Against the four goals: speed, nothing new runs and no header grows (the method-4 design's two stated costs, the once-flag and the hand-over routine, already exist in the text for every `ThreadShared` class and every `dyn` value); readability, the ordinary worker, server and library program is shorter than today (no concrete error type, no enum for two failures) and the one written word is on the thing it describes, the base class; safety, no one-thread owner can enter an `AnyError`, a `Result` error, a channel or a scoped task's `ref` through any class declared anywhere, each refusal falling on the class that holds the one-thread part, in its own package, with a line to write; consistency, the class clause now says what THR-8's definition ("nothing reachable from it") always said, the marker table and THR-9 agree with it, and the dyn clause and the class clause are one shape (the erased holder is judged by the declaration that erases it).
designs.remaining_doubt: (1) The clause "a `thread_shared T` of an open `T` is `Send` and `ThreadShared` whatever its class promises" rests on every route to a `thread_shared` object passing [THR-1]'s making-line check on the concrete class: `thread_shared x` on a value not made so is `E7017`, upcasts keep the word ([TYP-5] rule 8), and C never makes an Ember object; the lead should confirm hot-reload migration ([HR-15]) and a `retained` object given to C ([FFI-35a]) add no route. If any does, the clause goes and `thread_shared Script` is judged by the promise like a plain `Script`, at the cost of the second route. (2) The in-package inference for an `open` class no other package can subclass lets an added subclass with a `shares` field break a `thread.spawn` elsewhere in the same package, the message naming the subclass's field; verdict 86 accepted that shape inside a package for effects, and the alternative (a promise on every open class) writes a word where the package can see everything. The lead may prefer the promise everywhere for one rule with no split. (3) Whether `Send`/`ThreadShared` written in the header of a class that is neither `open` nor `abstract` should be an error (today's E3100/E2040, kept here) or a harmless redundancy; kept refused for consistency with "written only in bounds". (4) The E2040 placement for a non-generic type that implements `Error` and is not `Send` (at the `implements` line) against FFI-17d's E7015 at the class for `threads=any`: two codes for "a type does not meet a marker it promised"; here E2040 is an unsatisfied interface parent and E7015 a one-thread value where another thread may reach it, as the table already divides them, but the lead may unify. (5) std's own error types were checked by name only (plain fields in `io.Error`, `ParseError`, `CppError`, core.em's two derives); the implementer confirms each compiles under the new parents, and `SendError[T]`'s `Error` implementation takes the bound. (6) The reload row is the smallest statement; whether the promise belongs in [HR-11]'s schema sentence as well is the lead's placement.

scores.holes: No accepted program breaks a promise that I could build: the derived class is checked where it is declared ("checked where the derived class is declared, by the package that declares it, whichever package declares the base (`[BLD-16]`)"), a generic derived class falls under "meets with its own fields" (a type parameter has only what its `needs` give, `[TYP-17]`: "Inside a generic body only the operations the bounds provide are available"), the OWN-13 edit closes the method pin (`weakref this` in a `Send` family), and HR-44 covers the reload. Weak points, not holes: (a) the derived-class refusal is `E2040` while `[FFI-17d]` already refuses the same situation (a class that promised any-thread holding a one-thread field) with `E7015` ("`threads=any` requires the class to be `Send` and `ThreadShared` (`E7015` at the class, naming the field"), so one situation carries two codes; (b) every `open` class, private ones included, needs the word, though `[WK-18]` already judges a private family from "no derived class in this package has one, and no `pub` class of the family is `open` or `abstract`, so no other package derives from it"; (c) the reload sentence sits in HR-44 (worked-out facts) though the promise is a written word, and covers only a removed marker: an *added* marker lets the base's rebuilt code hand `Script`s to threads while a dependant's `Enemy(Script)` with `shares Level`, not rebuilt, was never checked; (d) `thread_shared Script()` on a promise-less `pub open class Script` compiles and can go nowhere, with no message naming the promise.

Safety hole in the text: "On a generic class the promise holds for each instance whose arguments meet the needs its parameters are bounded by, as a generic `unsafe extend` does". Program: gamekit `pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`; game `class Holder[T](Script):` with `item: T` and no bounds; `h = Holder[shares Level](shares level)`; `fail(owns h)?` into `AnyError`; `thread.spawn(owns fn() owns r: r.is_err())`. By that sentence `Holder[shares Level]` does not hold the promise, yet it is a `Script` (`[TYP-5]` rule 8) and the `Script`-typed value is `Send` by the header; the `shares` count races. (The implementer step 2 says the opposite, "A generic class checks with its parameters' written needs"; the rule text is what counts.) Ambiguity: "it is `Send` only when its header writes `implements Send`" leaves `pub open class GameError implements Error:` undecided as a promise, though IFC-3's edit assumes it. Consistency: TYP-43's edit makes `implements Send` on a final class or struct `E2040` while the `E3100` row ("`Send` declared by hand without `unsafe extend`") and TYP-43's own earlier sentence ("written without `unsafe` it is `E3100`") stay, so one program has two codes; the `E3100` row is not edited at all, and would still refuse the header promise it allows. HR-11's row covers a dropped promise only, not an added one.

Sound as far as I can break it, with one clause resting on a route the text does not close: "a `thread_shared T` ... of an `open` or `abstract` `T` whatever its class promises, since the line that makes a `thread_shared` object checks the object's own class". The making line checks the class as it is when compiled; a reload of the derived class's package that adds `level: shares Level = shares Level()` migrates a live `thread_shared Enemy`, upcast to `thread_shared Script` and already on another thread (made in a package the reload does not rebuild), into an object holding a `shares` owner; Annex B's table refuses a changed field type but says nothing of an added one-thread field on a class whose instances are `thread_shared`. That route is pre-existing for final classes too, so I score it as a doubt the design itself admits ("the lead should confirm hot-reload migration"), not a new hole; but the clause is a second rule a newcomer must hold ("a `thread_shared` of an open class is Send whatever the class says") for a small gain. Readability: the THR-8 clause is the longest of the three and admits two spellings ("in its header or in an `extend` of its own package") and a third promise route (`threads=any`). Consistency: the BLD-14 item 8 edit records the promise among "facts worked out", though it is a written word `[MOD-9]` already carries ("only the written word counts across the edge").

judgements.grafts: From design 2: the BLD-16 list gains the fact this ruling forbids (\"not by which classes a dependant derives from one of its `open` or `abstract` classes\"); the derived-class refusal is `E7015` at the class, naming the field, as `[FFI-17d]` and `[OWN-13]` already refuse a class that promised any-thread and holds a one-thread part (one situation, one code), leaving `E2040` for an `implements` line whose parent is unmet; `thread_shared` on a new object of a promise-less `pub open` class is `E7015` at the making line, naming the promise (verdict 165's shape, and design 1's doubt (1) answered); the in-package judgement of a class no other package can derive from, in `[WK-18]`'s exact words (\"no `pub` class of the family is `open` or `abstract`, so no other package derives from it\"), so a private hierarchy writes nothing, as `[EFF-2a]` already treats its virtual calls; and the HR-11 schema clause. From design 3: \"an interface that needs it\" named as a promise (`pub open class GameError implements Error:`), so the question design 2 left open is answered in THR-8; the Annex B table row for a promise \"added or removed\", widened so that an added promise is refused too; the DRV-1 sentence for `@derive` on a generic type (also design 2's). My own closing of design 2's hole, made explicit in THR-8: a generic derived class is checked under its written bounds, the message giving the bounded line. Not taken: design 3's `thread_shared T`-whatever-the-promise clause (a second rule, resting on a reload route Annex B does not close); design 3's `extend Script implements Send:` second spelling (one place, the header); design 3's BLD-14 item 8 edit (a written word, not a worked-out fact); design 1's HR-44 placement (replaced by HR-11 and the B.3 row, where \"base class changed | refused\" lives).

final_edits.rule: §IV.8 standard interfaces, the signature sketch (CURRENT-SPEC.md line 1958)
final_edits.old:
interface Error: needs (Debug, Display):
    fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]                            # default: None
final_edits.new:
interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):   # any thread may hold and read an error
    fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]                            # default: None
final_edits.why: The cause: every error is erased through `Error` (`dyn Error`, the box in `AnyError`, the default error of every `Result[T]`), and `[THR-8]` decides an erased value by its interface ("`dyn I` when `I` requires it (`interface I: needs Send:`)"); `Error` required only `Debug` and `Display`, so by the rules no `Result[int]` could leave its thread, which no rule said. This is the declaration every bound, every `dyn Error` and every implementer reads; std/src/core.em line 80 follows it.

final_edits.rule: TYP-17, the example of an interface's parents (line 1742)
final_edits.old: (`interface Error: needs (Debug, Display):`)
final_edits.new: (`interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):`)
final_edits.why: The second copy of the declaration; left as it was, the generics chapter would decide a program differently from §IV.8.

final_edits.old:
A class is final unless declared `open` or
  `abstract`.
final_edits.new:
A class is final unless declared `open` or
  `abstract`. An `open` or `abstract` class that another package may derive from says in its header
  whether any thread may hold its objects, `implements Send`, `implements ThreadShared`, or an
  interface that needs them (`[IFC-3]`): a promise every class derived from it keeps, checked where
  each is declared (`[THR-8]`, `[THR-9]`); a class that cannot be subclassed is judged from its
  fields, as a struct is.
final_edits.why: A reader of the class rules finds the header word where `open` and `abstract` are defined; the rule itself lives in `[THR-8]`, where `Send` is defined.

final_edits.old:
Structs, enums, tuples, fixed arrays, collections and class objects
  are `Send` when every component is; an `owns T` when `T` is;
final_edits.new:
Structs, enums, tuples, fixed arrays, collections and objects of a class
  that cannot be subclassed are `Send` when every component is, a class object's base fields and the
  kind its methods say (`[OWN-13]`) among them; **an object held by the type of an `open` or
  `abstract` class is judged by what the class declares**, since it may be of any class derived from
  it (`[TYP-5]` rule 8), in a package the holder's package never sees (`[BLD-16]`): it is `Send`
  when the class, or a base of it, writes `implements Send` in its header, or implements an
  interface that needs `Send` (`pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`, `pub open
  class GameError implements Error:`), a promise for the class and every class derived from it, as a
  method pins a class and its derived classes (`[OWN-13]`) and a weak count is carried by a whole
  family (`[OBJ-1]`); the same for `ThreadShared` (`[THR-9]`). The promise is checked where each
  class of the family is declared, by that class's own package, from the base's declaration in its
  interface file (`[MOD-9]`: a word exists, so only the written word counts), over the class's own
  fields and the kind its methods say, a generic class under its written bounds (a type parameter
  has the markers its `needs` give): a field or a method that breaks the promise is `E7015` at the
  class, naming the field, the promise and its line, and giving a copy line, and the `thread_shared`
  line only where no line then changes the value directly (`[THR-1]`, verdict 73) ("`Enemy` is a
  `Script`, whose objects any thread may hold (`pub open class Script implements Send,
  ThreadShared:`, gamekit/src/lib.em line 3), a promise every class derived from `Script` keeps, and
  `Enemy.level` (line 8) is a `shares Level`, an owner counted on one thread; keep what `Enemy` reads
  from the level by copy: write `level_name: String` in place of line 8, or share the level between
  threads: `level: thread_shared Level`"; for a generic class the message gives the bounded line,
  `[T: needs (Send, ThreadShared)]` above `class Holder(Script):`). A derived class may write a
  promise its base does not; it holds for it and its derived classes, never for the base. An object
  held by the type of an `open` or `abstract` class with no such promise is handed to no thread,
  whatever classes the program derives, which no package can see: at a hand-over by any route of
  `[THR-2]` it is `E7015` ("`s` is a `Script`, an `open` class whose objects may be of any class
  derived from it, and `Script` does not say any thread may hold them; write `pub open class Script
  implements Send:` (gamekit/src/lib.em line 3), after which every class derived from `Script` is
  checked for it where it is declared, or hand the object over by its own class, `d: Door`"), and
  `thread_shared Script()` is `E7015` at the making line with the same message (`[THR-1]`). An
  `open` or `abstract` class no other package can derive from (no `pub` class of its family is
  `open` or `abstract`, `[WK-18]`) needs no promise: its objects are judged from the fields and
  methods of every class its package derives from it, as a call through its `virtual` methods counts
  every override the package has (`[EFF-2a]`), and a refusal names the derived class and its field;
  an `owns T` when `T` is;
final_edits.why: This is the cause. "class objects are `Send` when every component is" counts the declared class's fields, narrower than THR-8's own definition ("nothing reachable from it"), and for an `open` class the components are a dependant's, a fact `[BLD-16]` forbids a package to read. The same shape the text already uses for the other erased holder (`dyn I` by its interface's `needs`), for a class's kind (`[OWN-13]`) and for the weak count (`[OBJ-1]`), and the one the owner chose for function types over a whole-program search (verdict 61). The check is local to the package that declares each class, needs no check at an upcast or a hand-over, and refuses the one-thread field at the class that holds it. `E7015` at the class is `[FFI-17d]`'s code for the same situation.

names the parent's associated type

  PoolFull[T] implements Error:`), never quietly for some arguments only (verdict 132), so

  or `sharedref mut` link, a `Cell`, an object held by the type of an `open` class that makes no
  promise, `[THR-8]`) is not an `Error`: `E2040` where it implements `Error`, naming the field and

  `Script`; write `pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:` (line 3), which every class
  derived from `Script` then keeps, or keep what the error reports by copy: `entity: int`"), and

final_edits.why: ERR-3 describes the declaration of §IV.8 and must say the same thing; the `Display + Debug` spelling was the pre-verdict-110 one. It states one property (any thread may hold an error) and leaves the placing of refusals to IFC-3 and DRV-1.

  nothing written (`[THR-10]`, `[THR-15]`, `[THR-1]`, `[THR-11]`). Nothing is checked at `?`: every

final_edits.new: `Send` declared by hand without `unsafe extend`, other than in the header of an `open` or `abstract` class, where it is a checked promise (`[TYP-43]`, `[THR-8]`);
final_edits.why: The row would otherwise refuse the promise TYP-43 now allows.

judgements.final_cost_row: No new row (`[COST-5]`): every judgement here is made when compiling, from a declaration the compiling package sees (the base's header in its own text or its interface file, the derived class's own fields, `Error`'s declared parents), and is covered by the existing row "What a function changes, reads and ends; the thread rules; the arena checks | not observable | all checked when compiling (`[EFF-24]`)". Two existing rows become reachable for an `AnyError` that now crosses, unchanged: "`?` converting an error into `AnyError` | guaranteed present, failure path only | one allocation (`[ERR-11]`)", and "An object handed whole to another thread | guaranteed present | ... one load and one test, then a call of the kind's hand-over routine, per owned value whose layout the handing package cannot see (held `dyn I`, of an `open` or `abstract` class, a function value's state)", which the boxed `dyn Error` pays once per `AnyError` handed to another thread, on the failure path only. The run-time alternative (a `Send` flag in `TypeInfo` tested at each hand-over of a base-typed object) was priced and turned down: it can only stop the program, since a `shares` owner inside the object cannot be moved away from its other owners.
judgements.owner_verdicts_touched: None overridden. 61 (a type says which threads may have its values, chosen over the compiler finding it from the whole program: kept and extended from function types to open classes, the header word). 94 (`thread.spawn` takes `thread_shared once fn() -> R`, `R` MUST be `Send`: unchanged, now met by `AnyError`). 110 (parents with `needs`: `interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):` in both copies). 108, 111, 113 (a `pub` generic and an `extend` write their needs; a derive writes its own: the generic error implementation writes `[T: needs (Send, ThreadShared)]` and the message gives the line). 132 (a declaration means what it says: `extend[T] X[T] implements Error:` is refused, never quietly narrowed). 73 (the given fix compiles: the copy line is always offered, `thread_shared` only where `[THR-1]` then holds). 86 and 122 (facts worked out from bodies: untouched; a marker is a property of a type, decided per `[BLD-16]`, lead ruling N76). 164, 165, 166 (a `sharedref mut` is neither marker; `thread_shared` refused where made; a scoped task touches no one-thread count: each error type or derived class holding one is refused where it is declared; 165's shape is reused for `thread_shared Script()`). 23 (a `shares` value never used from two threads: none can sit inside an error, a derived class of a promising family, or a base-typed value that crosses). 114 and 101 (a handed object's links say gone; the 32-byte header: `[THR-2]`'s routine already walks the boxed error). Lead rulings touched, reported: ODR-111 (`Send` by hand only as `unsafe extend`: kept for the vouch; the class header is a compiler-checked promise, so `[TYP-43]` names it without `unsafe`); ODR-255 (`dyn I` Send/Sync when `I` requires it: its `ThreadShared` half now written in `[THR-9]`); ODR-050 (a `Result`'s error parameter unbounded: kept, a one-thread type stays a `Result` error printed by `main`); N76 (`[BLD-16]`: the list gains one fact); N77 (`[OWN-13]`: one more contradiction in the same sentence). The owner gave no verdict on K20 itself (J6-16 was routed to him); this is the proposal, with its cost stated: an error type holding a one-thread part is refused where it implements `Error`, even in a one-thread program, the fix being a copy; a `pub open` class's objects cross threads only when its author writes the promise.
judgements.remaining_doubt: (1) `[CLS-12]`'s "On an object several threads reach, the kept result is filled once under a once-flag" is a whole-program fact as written; under `[BLD-16]` it should be read from the class's declaration (it promises `ThreadShared`, implements `Error`, or its methods pin it `thread_shared`). Pre-existing (the method-4 record's S2-2), made reachable by this ruling, not caused by it; no edit here, flagged for the lead. (2) A reload that adds a one-thread field with a default (`level: shares Level = shares Level()`) to a class whose live instances are `thread_shared` on other threads, made in a package the image does not rebuild: Annex B's table refuses a changed field type but says nothing of an added one; pre-existing for final classes, independent of this question, and the reason design 3's `thread_shared T`-whatever-the-promise clause was not grafted. (3) Two spellings reach one promise (`implements Send` directly, or `implements Command` with `interface Command: needs Send`); both exist in the grammar and both are checked by the one THR-8 sentence; a lead who wants one may refuse the bare marker when an interface in the list already brings it. (4) The in-package judgement of a class no other package can derive from lets an added subclass with a `shares` field break a `thread.spawn` elsewhere in the same package (the message names the subclass's field); verdict 86 accepted that shape inside a package for effects, and `[WK-18]` and `[EFF-2a]` already draw this exact line; a lead who wants one rule drops that sentence and requires the word on every `open` class. (5) `Error` requiring `ThreadShared` as well as `Send` refuses an error holding a `Cell` as an `Error`; `Send` alone would serve `spawn`, channels and joins, but `ref AnyError` to a scoped task and an `AnyError` under a `thread_shared` holder's lock (verdict 165's shape) would then be refused; both markers follow Rust's anyhow and Swift. (6) std must compile once under the new parents: `io.Error`, `ParseError`, `CppError` and core.em's two derived enums hold plain data; `SendError[T]` (std/src/sync.em 122) gets its `Error` implementation under `[T: needs (Send, ThreadShared)]`; `pub open class AnyStorage` (std/src/ecs.em 101) writes the promise only if a `World` is meant to cross threads (ODR-218); read only, not verified. (7) A base-typed value whose exact kind the compiler sees on the line (`s = Script()` handed over at once) is refused without the promise; a small flow rule would allow it, left out as not the smallest change (the `dyn I` cost already carried today).

scores.holes: Reload add route open: its HR-44 sentence refuses only "a reload whose new image removes a marker from it"; a reload of gamekit alone that changes `pub open class Script:` to `pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:` lets gamekit's new `thread.spawn(owns fn() owns s: ...)` with `s: Script` cross while the game's `class Enemy(Script): level: shares Level`, not rebuilt, was never checked; `[HR-44]` compares "what each function may change, read and end", not a header word. THR-8 is left saying "`Send` is inferred from the words and written only in bounds" and THR-9 "written only in bounds", and the table header "(`Send` written by hand only with `unsafe extend`, `[TYP-43]`)", each contradicting its CLS-4/TYP-43 edits. Its IFC-3 sentence checks a derived class for "a marker parent" of an interface the base implements; a base writing `implements Send` directly has `Send` as the interface, not a parent, and CLS-4 points to IFC-3 for that case while IFC-3 points back to THR-8. Its IFC-3 old text "(ODR-042)." occurs three times in the file. `thread_shared Script` for a promise-less `Script` is undecided (THR-8: "a `thread_shared T` ... when `T` is `Send` and `ThreadShared`" now reads not `Send`, so a checked `thread_shared Enemy()` upcast cannot cross). Its accepted program reads `d.entity` from the game while gamekit declares `let entity: int` without `pub`.

Its THR-8 old text does not match the file ("`Send`; a
  `thread_shared T`, and a
  `weakref thread_shared T`" where the file reads "`Send`; a `thread_shared T`, and a
  `weakref thread_shared T`"), so the cause edit cannot be applied as written. `implements Send` on a final class is `E2040` in its TYP-43 and E2040-row edits while the E3100 row's "`Send` declared by hand without `unsafe extend`" is left unchanged: two codes for one program. Reload: its HR-11 sentence covers "a new image that drops one from a class" only; the add route above is open. `open class GameError implements Error:` must also write `implements Send, ThreadShared` (its IFC-3: "An `open` or `abstract` class meets a marker parent through the promise in its header"; its step 2 collects only "the markers named in this header's `implements` list that are `Send` or `ThreadShared`"), two redundant words on every error hierarchy. Its step 3 reads "subclassable outside its package (`pub`)": a private `open class Base:` with `pub open class Mid(Base):` is derivable outside through `Mid`, so a `Base`-typed value judged from the package's own derived classes could hold a dependant's `Evil(Mid)` with a `shares` field; the rule text's "cannot be subclassed outside its package" is right only read transitively, which the step does not. THR-9's "written only in bounds" and the table header untouched. Cites verdict 132 (`@ffi(const)` overlays) as "a declaration means what it says".

THR-9's "It is inferred like `Send` and written only in bounds" and the table header "(`Send` written by hand only with `unsafe extend`)" untouched, both contradicting the header promise. Four spellings of one promise (header, `extend` in the class's package, an interface that needs the markers, `threads=any`): the `extend` spelling re-opens TYP-43's "`Send` by hand only as `unsafe extend`" for a memberless `extend Script implements Send:` that a reader tells from the vouch only by the class's being open. Its step 2(b) says "`open`/`abstract` and `pub`" where the rule says "no other package can subclass (`[EFF-2a]`)": the same narrow-step risk as design 2 (a private base with a `pub open` derived class). The `thread_shared T` clause inherits the existing reload gap (Annex B: "field added with a default | initialised to that default" on a class another package makes `thread_shared`), not caused by it. Cites verdict 132 wrongly, as design 2 does. Its THR-8 message offers `level: thread_shared Level` unconditionally, which compiles only where no line then changes the level directly (`[THR-1]`, verdict 73).

judgements.grafts: Winner: the third design (counting the JSON list from 1). All three put the same word on the same thing (an `open` or `abstract` class's header says whether any thread may hold its objects, `Error` needs `Send` and `ThreadShared`, `AnyError`'s markers follow from its fields) and the third is the one whose edits can be applied (its old texts match the file), that fixes THR-8's own \"written only in bounds\" sentence, that keeps `E3100` for `Send` on a final class, and that covers the reload add route (its Annex B row says \"added or removed\"), the route designs 1 and 2 leave open. Taken from the third and kept: the THR-8 class clause by its class (final by fields, derivable-outside by promise, private family by its package's derived classes as `[EFF-2a]` counts overrides), the promise through an interface that needs the markers (`open class GameError implements Error:` needs no second word), the `thread_shared T` clause (a `thread_shared` object is made only by a line that checks its own class, `E7017` elsewhere, so a checked `thread_shared Enemy()` upcast to `thread_shared Script` still crosses), THR-9's class and `dyn` clauses, BLD-14 item 8, the Annex B row, DRV-1's generic derive, IFC-3's generic implementation. Trimmed from the third: the `extend` spelling (the header is the one place, as TYP-43 keeps `unsafe extend` the one place for the vouch) and `threads=any` as a promise (FFI-17d already requires the class to be `Send` and `ThreadShared`, which for an open trampoline class now means the header word; noted under remaining doubt, FFI-17d unchanged); the mis-cited verdict 132 is dropped. Grafted from the second: the generic-class sentence (a promise on `open class Holder[T] implements Send:` holds per instance under the parameters' written needs, as a generic `unsafe extend` does), the BLD-16 list sentence (\"not by which classes a dependant derives from one of its `open` or `abstract` classes\"), the one-sentence pointer in CLS-4 where `open` and `abstract` are defined, the `E7015` message's two fixes (a copy line first, then `thread_shared` only where `[THR-1]` then holds), and the \"derived class may promise what its base does not\" sentence. Grafted from the first: the OWN-13 sentence (a method pinning a class one-thread while it or a base promises `Send` is the same contradiction as a class pinned both ways, `E7015` at the one-thread line), and the ERR-8 sentence that a refused one-thread error was refused where it was declared an error, never at the `?`. Added by the judge, missing from all three: the THR-9 \"written only in bounds\" carve-out, the marker table header's carve-out, the E9030 row entry, the transitive statement of \"another package may derive from it\" (it, or an `open` or `abstract` class derived from it in its package, is `pub`), and the interface-file record of a private open family's inferred markers (a dependant holding one through a `pub` type's private field reads them, `[BLD-14]` item 8).

final_edits.rule: §IV.8 standard interfaces, the signature sketch (the declaration ERR-3 and TYP-17 cite)
final_edits.old:
interface Error: needs (Debug, Display):
    fn source()
final_edits.new:
interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):      # any thread may hold and read an error ([ERR-3])
    fn source()
final_edits.why: This is the declaration every bound, every `dyn Error` and every implementer reads ("These are the definitions; `std.core` declares them"); `std/src/core.em` line 80 follows it. `Error` was the one erasing interface that said nothing about threads, so by `[THR-8]`'s "`dyn I` when `I` requires it" every erased error was a one-thread value and `Result[int]` could not leave its thread, which no rule said.

final_edits.rule: TYP-17, the example of an interface's parents
final_edits.old: (`interface Error: needs (Debug, Display):`)
final_edits.new: (`interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):`)
final_edits.why: The third copy of the declaration; left as it was, the generics chapter would decide a program differently from §IV.8 and `[ERR-3]`.

final_edits.old:
`Error` is the
  interface of error types: `Display + Debug` with `fn source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]` (default
  `None`) (§IV.8).
final_edits.new:
`Error` is the
  interface of error types, `interface Error: needs (Debug, Display, Send, ThreadShared):` with `fn
  source() -> Option[ref dyn Error]` (default `None`) (§IV.8): an error is a value any thread may
  hold and read, so `dyn Error`, and `AnyError` with it, are `Send` and `ThreadShared` (`[THR-8]`,
  `[THR-9]`, `[ERR-8]`), and a `Result` whose error is one goes to a worker thread, through a channel
  and into a scoped task's view as any such value does (`[THR-10]`, `[THR-15]`, `[THR-11]`,
  `[THR-2]`). A type holding a value that stays on one thread (a `shares` or `shares mut` owner, a
  `weakref T` or `sharedref mut` link, a `Cell`, an object held by the type of an `open` or
  `abstract` class another package may derive from whose header promises neither marker, `[THR-8]`)
  is not an `Error`: where it implements `Error` it is `E2040`, naming the field and giving the line
  that compiles (`[IFC-3]`: "`Error` needs `Send` and `ThreadShared`, since any thread may hold an
  error, and `LoadError.script` is a `Script`, an `open` class whose header does not say that any
  thread may hold its objects, so a `LoadError` may hold an object of a class another package
  derives from `Script`; keep what the error reports as a copy, `entity: int`, or write `pub open
  class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:` (line 3), which every class derived from `Script`
  then keeps"), and at `@derive(Error)` it is `E2080`, naming the field (`[DRV-1]`); it may still
  be a `Result`'s error, matched or printed by its `Display` (`[ERR-1]`, `[ERR-12]`, ODR-050), and
  it does not pass through `?` into `AnyError`.
final_edits.why: ERR-3 describes the declaration of §IV.8 and the two must say one thing; the `Display + Debug` spelling is the one verdict 110 replaced. It states one property (any thread may hold an error) and leaves the placing of refusals to IFC-3 and DRV-1; the message gives the copy line first, which always compiles (verdict 73), and the base's promise second.

final_edits.old:
An `AnyError` passed through `?` into another
  `AnyError` is handed over (`[ERR-7]`).
final_edits.new:
An `AnyError` passed through `?` into another
  `AnyError` is handed over (`[ERR-7]`). `AnyError` is `Send` and `ThreadShared` as its parts are:
  its `owns dyn Error` because `Error` requires both (`[ERR-3]`, `[THR-8]`, `[THR-9]`), its identity
  a number, its context a list of `String`; so a worker returns `Result[int]` through `thread.spawn`
  or a channel, a `thread_shared` holder keeps one under its lock and a scoped task reads one through
  `ref`, with nothing written (`[THR-10]`, `[THR-15]`, `[THR-1]`, `[THR-11]`). Nothing is checked at
  `?`: every `E: needs Error` met the requirement where it implemented `Error`, in its own package,
  so the one-thread error an `AnyError` cannot carry was refused there, never at the `?`; an
  `AnyError` handed to another thread walks the error it holds by that error's kind's hand-over
  routine, as any `owns dyn I` value is walked (`[THR-2]`).
final_edits.why: The question asked for `AnyError`'s markers in so many words, and ERR-8 is where `AnyError` is defined; the sentence states a consequence of ERR-3 and THR-8, adds no rule of its own, and names the one run-time step that already exists (THR-2's routine for a `dyn` value, a row of §X.4).

final_edits.rule: THR-8, the class-object clause of the `Send` list (the cause)
final_edits.old:
Structs, enums, tuples, fixed arrays, collections and class objects
  are `Send` when every component is; an `owns T` when `T` is;
final_edits.new:
Structs, enums, tuples, fixed arrays and collections
  are `Send` when every component is; a class object by its class, since an object held by a base
  class type may be of any class derived from it (`[TYP-5]` rule 8): an object of a class that is
  neither `open` nor `abstract` when the class's fields, inherited ones included, are; an object of
  an `open` or `abstract` class that **another package may derive from** (it, or an `open` or
  `abstract` class derived from it in its package, is `pub`) only when the class **promises** it in
  its header, `implements Send`, `implements ThreadShared`, or an interface that needs them (`pub
  open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`, `open class GameError implements Error:`),
  written without `unsafe` since the compiler checks it (`[TYP-43]`): the promise holds the class's
  own fields and methods (`[OWN-13]`) and those of every class derived from it, each checked where
  that class is declared, by the package that declares it, from the base's declaration in its
  source or in its interface file (`[MOD-9]`, `[BLD-14]` item 8), so a derived class that breaks it
  is `E7015` at its own line, naming the field and the promise and giving a copy line, and the
  `thread_shared` line only where `[THR-1]` then holds ("`Enemy.level` is a `shares Level` owner,
  which stays on one thread, and `Script` promises that any thread may hold its objects (`pub open
  class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`, gamekit/src/lib.em line 3), a promise every class
  derived from it keeps; keep what the enemy reads from the level as a copy, `level_name:
  String`"); a derived class may promise what its base does not, for itself and the classes
  derived from it, never for the base; a generic class's promise holds for each instance whose
  arguments meet the needs its parameters are bounded by, as a generic `unsafe extend` does
  (`[TYP-43]`); an object of such a class whose header promises nothing is one no thread may be
  handed, whatever classes the program derives, which no package can see (`[BLD-16]`): a value held
  by its type reaching another thread by any route of `[THR-2]` is `E7015` at that line ("`s` is a
  `Script`, an `open` class whose header does not say that any thread may hold its objects, so it
  may be an object of a class another package derives from `Script`; write `pub open class Script
  implements Send:` (gamekit/src/lib.em line 3), after which every class derived from `Script` is
  checked for it where it is declared, or hand the object over by its own class, `d: Door`"); and
  an object of an `open` or `abstract` class that no other package can derive from when its fields
  and those of every class its package derives from it are, with nothing written, as a call through
  its `virtual` methods counts every override the package has (`[EFF-2a]`), a refusal naming the
  derived class and its field; an `owns T` when `T` is;
final_edits.why: This is the cause. "class objects are `Send` when every component is" counted the declared class's fields, narrower than THR-8's own definition ("nothing reachable from it"), and for a class another package may derive from the components are a fact `[BLD-16]` forbids a package to read. The family's markers become a word of the class's own declaration, checked at every class's own line by the package that sees its fields: local to each package, no check at an upcast, a hand-over or a `?`, and the refusal falls on the class that holds the one-thread field. It is the shape the text already uses for `dyn I` (`needs Send`), for a class's kind (`[OWN-13]`) and for the weak count (`[OBJ-1]`), the one the owner chose for function types over a whole-program search (verdict 61), and `[EFF-2a]`'s split for a family no other package can reach.

final_edits.old:
a `thread_shared T`, and a
  `weakref thread_shared T`, when `T` is `Send` and `ThreadShared`;
final_edits.new:
a `thread_shared T`, and a
  `weakref thread_shared T`, when `T` is `Send` and `ThreadShared`, and for an `open` or `abstract`
  `T` whatever its class promises, since a `thread_shared` object is made only by a line that checks
  the object's own class (`[THR-1]`, verdict 165; `E7017` anywhere else) and an upcast keeps the
  word (`[TYP-5]` rule 8);
final_edits.why: Without it the class clause would make `thread_shared Script` not `Send` for a promise-less `pub open class Script`, though every `thread_shared Enemy()` was checked at its making line; the clause keeps a polymorphic object that must cross threads (`script: thread_shared Script`) without forcing the promise on every subclass, and decides a question an implementer would otherwise guess.

final_edits.rule: THR-8, "`Send` is inferred from the words"
final_edits.old:
`Send` is inferred from the words and written only
  in bounds;
final_edits.why: The sentence would otherwise contradict the clause added above.

final_edits.new:
It is inferred
  like `Send` and written only in bounds (`[T: needs ThreadShared]` above `fn keep(xs: Array[T]) ->
  int:`), in the header of an `open` or `abstract` class as a checked promise (`[THR-8]`,
  `[TYP-43]`) and in messages;
final_edits.why: None of the three designs touched it; left as it was, THR-9 would refuse the `implements ThreadShared` that THR-8 and TYP-43 allow.

final_edits.old: Structural types are `ThreadShared` when every component is.
final_edits.new:
Structural types are `ThreadShared` when every component is; a class object as `[THR-8]` judges
  `Send`: by its fields when its class is neither `open` nor `abstract`, by the class's promise
  (`implements ThreadShared`, or an interface that needs it) when another package may derive from
  it, each derived class checked where it is declared (`E7015`), and by its package's derived
  classes when none can; `dyn I` when `I` requires it (`interface I: needs ThreadShared:`), as for
  `Send` (ODR-255), so `dyn Error` is (`[ERR-3]`); a `thread_shared T` and a `weakref thread_shared
  T` of an `open` or `abstract` `T` whatever its class promises, as `[THR-8]` says.
final_edits.why: THR-9 had no words for a class object and none for a `dyn`, so `ref r` of a `Result[int]` given to a scoped task (`ref T` is `Send` when `T` is `ThreadShared`, `[THR-8]`) and an `AnyError` under a `thread_shared` holder's `RwLock` (verdict 165) were undecided; ODR-255 ruled the `dyn` half and the text never wrote it.

final_edits.old: **Marker interfaces**, derived automatically (`Send` written by hand only with `unsafe extend`, `[TYP-43]`):
final_edits.new: **Marker interfaces**, derived automatically (`Send` written by hand only with `unsafe extend`, and `Send` and `ThreadShared` as the checked promise in the header of an `open` or `abstract` class, `[TYP-43]`):
final_edits.why: The header would otherwise contradict the edited TYP-43; none of the three designs touched it.

final_edits.old: a class object is when its fields are;
final_edits.new: a class object is when its fields are, where its class is neither `open` nor `abstract`; an object held by the type of an `open` or `abstract` class another package may derive from only when the class's header promises `Send` (`implements Send`, or an interface that needs it), which every class derived from it is checked against where it is declared, and one held by the type of such a class no other package can derive from when the fields of every class its package derives from it are (`[THR-8]`); `dyn I` when `I` requires it;
final_edits.why: `[TYP-43]` says "the table answers them": the row was the narrow reading that let a base-class value holding a one-thread derived object through, and it must give THR-8's answer.

final_edits.old: every component is `ThreadShared` (the `ref A` a value made in a manager's instance holds included, `[TYP-46a]`);
final_edits.new: every component is `ThreadShared` (the `ref A` a value made in a manager's instance holds included, `[TYP-46a]`); a class object as for `Send`, by its class's header promise (`implements ThreadShared`, or an interface that needs it) where another package may derive from it, each derived class checked where it is declared (`[THR-9]`); `dyn I` when `I` requires it;
final_edits.why: The row named neither a class object nor a `dyn`; it must agree with THR-9.

final_edits.old:
A program writes `Send` by
  hand, for a struct or enum of its own package that holds a raw pointer, only as `unsafe extend T
  implements Send:` with no members and a `# SAFETY:` note, taking the responsibility the compiler
  cannot check
final_edits.new:
A program writes `Send` or `ThreadShared` in one checked place, the header of an `open` or
  `abstract` class (`pub open class Script implements Send, ThreadShared:`), a promise about every
  class derived from it that the compiler checks at each class's declaration (`[THR-8]`,
  `[THR-9]`), so it needs no `unsafe`; on a generic class it holds for each instance whose arguments
  meet the needs its parameters are bounded by; on a struct, an enum or a class that is neither
  `open` nor `abstract`, whose markers are inferred, the word is refused as below (`E3100` for
  `Send`: "`Door` cannot be subclassed, so whether any thread may have a `Door` is read from its
  fields; remove `implements Send`"; `E2040` for `ThreadShared`). Otherwise a program writes `Send`
  by hand, for a struct or enum of its own package that holds a raw pointer, only as `unsafe extend
  T implements Send:` with no members and a `# SAFETY:` note, taking the responsibility the compiler
  cannot check
final_edits.why: TYP-43 refused every hand-written marker but the `unsafe extend` vouch; the header promise is a bound the compiler checks for every class of the family, as `interface I: needs Send` is, not a vouch, so it is allowed without `unsafe` and refused where inference already answers, with today's codes. The grammar's `class_decl := ["open" | "abstract"] "class" IDENT ["(" type ")"] [implements]` already parses it; no new syntax.

final_edits.old:
A class is final unless declared `open` or
  `abstract`.
final_edits.new:
A class is final unless declared `open` or
  `abstract`. An `open` or `abstract` class that another package may derive from says in its header
  whether any thread may hold its objects, `implements Send`, `implements ThreadShared`, or an

The `@cached` row's clause \"on an object several threads reach, the result is filled once under a once-flag\" now reaches a `@cached` method of a class whose objects any thread may have (one that promises `ThreadShared`, or implements `Error`), a clause that already existed for every `ThreadShared` class. The run-time alternative was priced and turned down: a `Send` flag in the kind's `TypeInfo` tested at each hand-over of a base-typed object costs one load and one test but can only stop the program, since a `shares` owner inside the object cannot be moved away from its other owners (docs/AUTOPILOT.md §4, \"A panic has to make sense\").

rulings.title: Where and when does a queued thread_shared value's drop run, and how is a wait inside a held lock in a with scope block kept from hanging when a task makes a value another thread lets go of?

designs.question: K10: where and when does a queued `thread_shared` value's drop run, and how is a wait inside a held lock in a `with scope` block kept from hanging when a task's thread made a value (a `Conn` travelling inside a plain `Batch`) that another thread lets go of, so that the value is queued for the task's thread, whose last check point is reached while the parent waits at the scope's end holding the lock (method 4's open objection E3-1)? Angle: speed first, then safety.
designs.summary: The hang is closed when compiling, at its cause: a task's (or job's, or `@parallel` chunk's) thread empties its own queue at its end, before its end is let go to the parent, so `[THR-11]` now says the task's function counts as possibly running the `drop` of every `thread_shared` value made on its thread and not handed over, from the making line to the task's end; `[THR-19]`'s existing clause ("the end of a `with scope` block, whose task changes what the held lock guards") then refuses the scope's end inside `with pool.lock:` as `E7018`, and `[THR-20]`'s `E7012` list stays as it is (a task is not "another thread"), which removes the contradiction method 4 left. Nothing runs for that rule. For the rest of K10 the ruling keeps method 4's decisions (no queued drop runs inside a lock, a walk, a view or a contract; a sleeping job worker is woken) but makes the mechanism `[BLD-16]`-clean and cheaper: one plain thread-local hold count maintained only by the places that keep drops out (a lock block or guard life, a walk or view rooted in a `static mut`, a function with a contract, a scope whose task touches an unguarded `static mut`), a check point empties the queue only when the hold is zero, the leaving that returns it to zero is a check point, back-edge check points exist only in loops that call or read an `Atomic`, and a worker ending a value outside a job whose `drop` reaches an unguarded `static mut` hands it, dead, to the main thread's queue instead of counting such values atomically from birth.

edits.new:
**A task's queue.** A `thread_shared` value made on a task's or a job's thread, by its body or a
  function it runs, and not handed over (`[RC-4]` point 4) is ended at that thread's check points, the
  last of them at the task's end, before its end is let go to the parent (`[RC-4]` point 3). So the
  task's function counts as possibly running the `drop` of every such value, from its making line to
  the task's end (`[DRP-8]`), and what those `drop`s change is the task's own change, checked as any
  other: against the parent and the other tasks until its join (`E7007`), at a start inside a walk of
  it (`E3020`), and at a wait for the task inside a lock those `drop`s take (`E7018`, `[THR-19]`). It is
  not a change made on another thread: `[THR-20]`'s `E7012` does not apply to it, since the task runs
  beside the main thread only until its join, and a value queued to its thread after that is ended by
  the thread that ends its last owner or, on a job worker, as `[RC-4]` point 3 says. A `jobs.scope()`
  job (`[JOB-2]`) and a `@parallel` chunk (`[PAR-2]`) are tasks for this rule.
edits.why: This is where E3-1 is caused: method 4 placed the task's last check point before its join is let go and relied on `[THR-20]` to count it, but `[THR-20]`'s list of functions that may run on another thread rightly excludes scoped tasks (they may reach main's `static mut`). The count belongs with the rule that defines what a task does and checks it until its join (verdict 104), so `[THR-19]`, `[THR-5]`, `E7007` and `E3020` all read it by their existing words, and `E7012` keeps its list. It is a property (what the task's thread may end), not a shape; nothing runs for it.

edits.old: `drop` runs where the last owner ends.** The last owner of a `thread_shared` value may end on any
edits.new:
`drop` runs where the last owner ends**, or, for a value queued back to the thread that made it
  (`[RC-4]` point 2), at a check point of that thread, where its hold is zero (`[RC-4]` point 3). The
  function of a thread other than the main one that makes such a value, by its lines or a function it
  runs, holds a count of it from the making line to the thread's last check point; a scoped task's or
  job's function the same, judged by `[THR-11]`. The last owner of a `thread_shared` value may end on any
edits.why: The headline was untrue for every queued value; the added clause makes the next sentence ("a function that may run on another thread and holds such a count counts as possibly running that value's `drop`") reach a spawned thread's own values, which closes method 4's E2-1 and lets `[THR-19]` judge `h.join()` under a lock, while the scoped case is sent to `[THR-11]` and not to this rule's list.

edits.old: A `drop` may change things outside its object (a log line, leaving a list).
edits.new:
A `drop` may change things outside its object (a log line, leaving a list). The ends at a check
  point in a function's lines (`[RC-4]` point 3) run only where the thread's hold is zero, outside every
  place that keeps them out, and are not part of that function's effects (`[EFF-1]`) or summary
  (`[EFF-24]`); what a thread's, task's or job's function may end at its last check point is counted
  in it as `[THR-20]` and `[THR-11]` say.
edits.why: `[EFF-1]` and `[EFF-24]` reach every drop through this rule; without the sentence every function with a check point would count the drops of every type its thread may queue (a whole-program fact, `[BLD-16]`), making walks across a looping call `E3020` and `@noblock` loops `E4003`. The last clause names both counting rules, so no function is counted by one and uncounted by the other (E3-1's contradiction).

edits.old: `System` keeps the two counts, its block waits for the check point and nothing reuses it.
edits.new:
`System` keeps the two counts, its block waits for the check point and nothing reuses it. A
     `thread_shared` value made inside a function with a contract that forbids an effect of its type's
     `drop` (`@noblock` and a `drop` that takes a lock, `@noalloc` and one that allocates, `[EFF-5]`) is
     marked handed over at its making line too, decided from that function's own declaration: its
     thread's check points are kept out of the function (point 3), which may never return, so its
     `drop` runs where its last owner ends, on the thread that ends it.
edits.why: Point 4 is the rule that moves the making thread's count into the away count; a value whose maker can never run its drop belongs there. Method 4's second condition (a drop reaching a module variable of the main thread, made in a job) is no longer needed: point 3 hands such a value to the main thread's queue instead, with no atomic count from birth.

edits.old:
3. **Check points.** The compiler places them: at every loop's back edge, before and after every
     call that may block the thread (waiting for a lock, a `join`, the end of a `with scope` block,
     a channel's receive, a sleep) and when the thread ends; the one after a `join` or a scope's end
     makes a value a joined task ended on its own thread end before the parent's next line.
edits.new:
3. **Check points.** The compiler places them: at the back edge of every loop whose body makes a
     call or reads an `Atomic` (a loop that may wait for another thread; a loop of plain operations on
     this thread's own values has none, and its end is the next point), before and after every call
     that may block the thread (waiting for a lock, a `join`, `jobs.wait`, the end of a `with scope`
     block, a channel's receive, a sleep), when a call C made into Ember returns to C, at the end of
     every task, job and `@parallel` chunk a thread runs, before its end is let go to what waits for
     it (its `join`, its scope's end), and when the thread ends; a job worker waiting for work waits
     at one, and a value put in its empty queue wakes it. Emptying the queue ends, on this thread, the
     values whose counts add up to zero (point 2) and runs their `drop`s there: it is a call of the
     `drop`s of every value that may be in this thread's queue, the `thread_shared` values made on this
     thread, by its own lines or a function it runs, that were not handed over (point 4) (`[DRP-8]`,
     `[WK-3]`). **Where the queue is emptied.** Each thread keeps one plain thread-local count, its
     hold: +1 where it enters a place a queued `drop` may not run inside and -1 where it leaves it, the
     places being a lock's `with` block or a guard's life (`[THR-18]`, `[THR-3]`: the `drop` may take
     that lock), a walk or a view rooted in a `static mut`, from its start to its last use (the `drop`
     may change it, `[BRW-18]`, `[THR-20]`), a function with a contract, from its entry to its return
     (`[EFF-5]`), and a `with scope` block whose task may read or change a `static mut` not guarded by a
     lock (`[THR-11]`); a check point empties the queue only when the hold is zero, and the leaving
     that takes it back to zero is a check point, so a queued value is ended at the thread's first
     point outside every such place, and never waits for a lock this thread holds, changes what it
     walks or views, or breaks a contract it is under. The add and subtract are omitted for a place
     that can reach no check point (a lock block of field accesses, a leaf function with a contract),
     decided from the place's own lines and its callees' summaries (`[EFF-24]`); nothing here is
     decided by a caller or by the program as a whole (`[BLD-16]`). What the queue ends has no owner
     and no opened name left (a name opened from a `weakref thread_shared T` link holds a count,
     `[RC-5]` point 2, and a `weakref T` link reaches no `thread_shared` value, `[THR-2]`), so no view

designs.accepted_program:
import std.thread
from std.sync import Atomic, Lock

static DONE: Atomic[int] = Atomic(0)

class Pool:
    lock: Lock = Lock()
    free: Array[int] guarded by lock = []

class Conn:
    id: int
    pool: thread_shared Pool
    fn drop():
        with this.pool.lock:
            this.pool.free.push(owns copy of this.id)

class Batch:
    conns: Array[thread_shared Conn] = []

class Inbox:
    lock: Lock = Lock()
    items: Array[Batch] guarded by lock = []

fn close_all(inbox: thread_shared Inbox):
    while DONE.load() == 0:
        with inbox.lock:
            inbox.items.clear()
    with inbox.lock:
        inbox.items.clear()

fn open_one(pool: thread_shared Pool, inbox: thread_shared Inbox):
    with inbox.lock:
        inbox.items.push(owns Batch(conns=[thread_shared Conn(id=1, pool=thread_shared pool)]))

fn main():
    pool = thread_shared Pool()
    inbox = thread_shared Inbox()
    closer = thread.spawn(owns fn() thread_shared inbox: close_all(inbox))
    with s = thread.scope():                  # the scope ends outside the pool's lock
        s.spawn(owns fn(): open_one(pool, inbox))
    DONE.store(1)
    closer.join()
    with pool.lock:
        println(pool.free.len())

# Compiles and prints `1`, on every run. Two timings, one outcome:
# - the closer clears the inbox before the task ends: the Conn goes to the task thread's queue; the task's
#   last check point (hold zero, before its end is let go) runs Conn's drop, takes pool.lock (free), pushes 1;
# - the closer clears after the task ended: the task thread's queue is closed ([RC-4] point 3), so the
#   closer ends the Conn at once and its drop pushes 1 on the closer's thread; close_all holds a count of
#   the Conn through the inbox, so [THR-20] counts that drop in it: it takes a Pool's lock, not the Inbox's
#   lock the closer holds, and reaches no module variable, so nothing is refused.
# Also still accepted, unchanged: J7-01's program (main holds pool.lock while walking pool.free, and a
# worker lets go of a Conn main made): the inner walk's back edge is inside a lock block, where main's
# hold is one, so the queue is not emptied there; the end of the `with pool.lock:` block takes the hold to
# zero and is a check point: Conn's drop runs there, pushes 1, and later frames and `h.join()` print 1.

For the K10 mechanism carried with it, row "A `thread_shared` value's two counts" of §X.4 as edited: one thread-local load and a branch per check point, placed at the back edge of a loop that calls or reads an `Atomic` (none in a loop of plain operations, so leaf loops keep C's code and vectorise), around a blocking call, at a task's, job's or chunk's end before its end is let go, at a thread's end, at a return to C and at a worker's idle wait; one plain add and one subtract of the thread's hold count per lock block or guard life, walk or view rooted in a `static mut`, function with a contract, or scope block whose task touches an unguarded `static mut`, only where the place may reach a check point (omitted for a block of plain field accesses or a leaf contract function), and one test of the hold only on the path where the queue is found non-empty; one futex wake for the first value put in an idle worker's empty queue; one push onto the main thread's queue for a value a worker ends outside a job whose drop reaches an unguarded `static mut`; atomic counts from the making line only for a value made `using` an instance or inside a contract function whose contract forbids an effect of its drop. designs.implementer_steps:
1. Summaries (`[EFF-24]`, written to interface files `[EFF-4]`/`[MOD-9]`): for each class with a `drop`, record what the drop may take (locks), change (`static mut`s, guarded fields), end, block or allocate; emit one bit in the type's table, "drop reaches an unguarded `static mut`". For each function, record (a) the set of `thread_shared` types it makes whose owner may travel (a making line, or a callee that makes one, where not every path stores the owner at a point-4 place or ends it on this thread; when unsure, it may travel), and (b) "may reach a check point" (it has one, or calls a function whose summary has the bit).
2. Effects of a unit of another thread (`thread.spawn`'s and `jobs.submit`'s function, a scoped task's or job's body, a `@parallel` chunk): add the drops of its may-travel types (its own and its callees', `[DRP-8]`) to the unit's effect set, from the making line to the unit's end. `[EFF-26]` carries them to the spawn or submit; `[THR-19]` reads them at a join, `jobs.wait` or scope end under a lock (`E7018`), `[THR-11]` against the parent and the other tasks (`E7007`) and at a start inside a walk (`E3020`), `[THR-20]` for an unscoped unit's module variables (`E7012`), the contract checker for a wait inside a contract. In-body check points contribute nothing to any summary (`[DRP-8]`).
3. Check-point placement, per function, from its own lines only: a back edge of a loop whose body contains a call or an `Atomic` read; before and after a blocking call; the unit's end (emitted before the join's release: the task stores its result and empties its queue, then signals); the thread's end; the return of a C entry (`[FFI-22]`); the worker's idle wait. Each is `if (tls->queue) ember_rt_drain(tls);`.
4. Hold places, per function: at the entry of a lock block or guard life, a `static mut` walk or view (its root is a `static mut`, read from the expression and from a view's `static` region), a function with a contract, and a scope block whose tasks' summaries touch an unguarded `static mut`, emit `tls->hold++`; at the exit `if (--tls->hold == 0 && tls->queue) ember_rt_drain(tls);`. Omit both where the place's lines and its callees' "may reach a check point" bits show no point inside. A generator paused inside a `static mut` walk keeps the increment until the walk ends or the generator is ended.
5. Runtime (`ember_rt.h`, M9): `ember_rt_drain` returns at once if `hold != 0`; otherwise pops the queue (an acquire, `[RT-8]`) and for each value adds home into away; sum zero: if this thread is a job worker outside a job and the type bit is set, push the value marked dead onto the main thread's queue, else run the drop and free with point 2's compare-exchange; sum positive: move home into away, clear queued, set handed over. Main's drain runs dead entries' drops directly. A push onto a worker's queue that finds the idle mark in the queue word does one futex wake. A thread's end: exchange the queue head with CLOSED after a final drain (a task's end does this before signalling its join).
6. Point 4 at making lines: emit the handed-over mark at the making line for a value made `using` an instance (already) and for a value made inside a declared-contract function whose contract forbids an effect of the type's drop (the function's own attribute and the type's summary; no caller fact).
7. Separate compilation and hot reload: every decision above reads the function's own lines, the type's interface summary and callees' summaries (`[BLD-16]`); the queue, the hold and the idle mark live in the thread's runtime record (`[HR-3a]`), not in the image, so a reload keeps them; a frame below a reload checkpoint runs its old code to its exit (`[HR-3b]`), so each increment meets its decrement; a dead value's drop runs the current code from the type's table. FFI: a host thread's hold is zero at its return to C (Ember regions close before a return), so the return's check point drains; values let go while the thread is in C follow method 4's decision 4, left to the owner.
8. Tests: the refused program (E7018 at the scope's end, the message above); the accepted program (prints 1); the same with `h.join()` on the task's handle under the lock (E7018); a task whose made value's drop pushes to an unguarded `static mut` the parent reads during the scope (E7007); J7-01's program (compiles, drop at the lock block's end); J7-02's program (workers woken, two textures freed right after the clear); a worker-made value whose drop pushes main's `static mut`, let go by main after the scope (ended on main, counted once); break tests removing each of steps 2, 4 and 5.
designs.departs_from_verdict: None. Verdict 101 is kept: the making thread deletes a queued value at a check point the compiler places, always before the thread ends (a task's or job's thread at its end, before its end is let go), or the thread that ends the last owner deletes it at once when the maker has ended; the hand-over at a making line under a contract is fix 2 taken where the compiler sees the maker can never end it; the dead value a worker hands to main is deleted by the maker's own drain, which only runs the drop elsewhere. Verdict 43 kept: every wait for a held lock is refused when compiling (the hold count tests no wait; it schedules the drain, as the queue test already does, and the hang program is E7018). Verdict 57 kept: an end counts as a call of the drop where it is placed, and a unit's last check point is in its function; in-body points are left out of a summary only because the hold keeps them where no rule's premise holds. Verdict 104 kept: a task's claims, its queued drops included, are checked until its join. Verdicts 56, 114, 122, 165, 166 untouched. Verdict 86 kept (nothing is written by the programmer). Verdict 88 is not needed here (no copies). Alternative considered and not applied, marked "departs from verdict 101": the task's end hands its non-empty queue to the parent (one atomic splice on that rare path), and the parent ends the values at its next check point outside its hold places; it refuses nothing, but a third thread, not the maker and not the one that ended the last owner, deletes the value, and not at once. designs.trade_offs: Speed: nothing new runs for the hang's closing; the carried mechanism costs a thread-local load and branch only in loops that already call or read an atomic (leaf loops lose the per-iteration test the current text charges them, a gain), two plain thread-local adds per lock block or contract function that may reach a check point (next to the lock's own atomic, or the call, these are noise), and one wake or one queue push on rare paths; given up: method 4's zero-instruction placement, which needed a copy of a function per call place and a whole-program fact a prebuilt library cannot have. Readability: one refusal where the program may hang (a scope's end or join under a lock the task's queued drops take), with a one-line fix in the message, like verdict 43's "a different Log is refused too"; a queued drop's visible effect may come a little later, at the end of the lock block, walk, view or contract the thread is in, and a task's drop at its end is now part of what the task does, so a parent that reads an unguarded `static mut` the drop changes during the scope is E7007 (a real race). Safety: never compromised; no drop runs inside a lock it takes, a walk or view it changes, or a contract it breaks; what the queue ends has no owner, so no view reads it; a worker's drop touching main's module variable runs on main. Consistency: one place (RC-4 point 3) places every hidden end, THR-11 and THR-20 together say which function is charged with a thread's last point, and DRP-8 names both, so no program is refused by one rule and compiled by another. Residual accepted: a value made by a helper called from a contract function that never returns waits for that function's return (the helper has no declared contract, and a caller fact may not decide its code).
designs.remaining_doubt: (1) Whether `thread.scope()` tasks run on threads of their own that end at the join or on job workers is not stated; the text is written to hold either way (an ended thread's values go to whoever ends the last owner; a living worker's are drained at its idle wait, with the hand to main for module variables), but the lead should pin it, since the two paths run the drop on different threads. (2) Verdict 43's "nothing is checked while running": the hold test runs only on the path where the queue is non-empty and tests no wait, so I read it as kept, but the owner may see any run-time branch in a lock block as a check; if so, method 4's per-place copies are the only alternative and they conflict with `[BLD-16]` for prebuilt libraries. (3) The "may travel" judgement at a making line is an over-approximation: where the compiler cannot prove every owner reaches a point-4 place, the task's function is charged with the drop, which may refuse a scope's end under a lock that could not hang in practice. (4) A generator paused inside a walk of a `static mut` holds the count across its suspension; a `Send` generator moved to another thread would carry a hold it cannot release there, so such a generator should not be `Send`, which `[THR-8]` does not yet say. (5) Method 4's decision 4 (a value queued to a host thread that has returned to C) stays with the owner; the hold is zero at a return to C, so option a (freed at the next call into Ember) needs no new mechanism, and option b (whoever lets go frees it while the thread is in C) needs one atomic step per return to C. (6) The hand of a dead value to main's queue assumes main is alive; when main has returned the process ends (`[THR-16]`), so no drop is owed. (7) The cost of two thread-local adds in a lock block that calls a looping library function was not measured; it should be priced against the lock's own cost on the P-cores before the row's words are final.

designs.summary: The queue is made harmless instead of the check points being made clever: a `thread_shared` value is marked handed over at the line that makes it (the mark `[RC-4]` point 4 already sets for a value made `using` an instance) in two more cases, decided by a property, never by a program's shape: (A) its type is not plain (its `drop`, or that of anything it owns all the way down, `thread_shared` owners included, has an effect a contract may forbid, reaches a `static mut`, or runs code the compiler cannot read whole), and (B) it is made on any thread but the main thread or a `thread.spawn` thread (a scope's task or job, a worker's chunk, a host thread), whose end no `join` waits for and whose claims the rules judge only until the join.
